report: Russian speaks of love in a sorcerer’s vocabulary. Ocharovat, to charm, comes from chary, “spells”. Privorozhit, to win with a love spell, from vorozhit, “to work magic”. Prelstit, to seduce, from lest, which once meant “deceit”. Plenit, to captivate, from plen, “captivity”; privyazannost, attachment, from privyazat, “to tie up”. Popular readings call 18-6-15 the “Dark Magician”: in the legend, someone in a past life used secret knowledge to cast love spells and bend others’ will. The legend cannot be checked; numbers are silent about past lives. But this tail needs no candles. It already lies in ordinary words about love: spells are the Moon at the entry, love the Lovers in the middle, captivity and the tether the Devil at the root.

Etymology proves nothing about numbers. But it shows that the dark magic here is no occult gift but an ordinary human one: being liked, drawing people in, staying on someone’s mind. Yet the cards hold magic too. Among Waite’s divinatory meanings for the Moon are “darkness”, “deception” and “occult forces”. Benebell Wen calls the Moon the signifier for society’s “magi, priest, or shaman”: the moon pulls on the water, and when the card appears in a reading, an “external invisible force” pulls on the person. A spell is exactly that: an invisible pull.

report.h3: The one who holds the chain is chained too

report: Waite’s key line about the Devil is not about magic. He describes a man and a woman chained to the altar, “as if Adam and Eve after the Fall”. And then: “he who is exalted above them is not to be their master for ever. Even now, he is also a bondsman, sustained by the evil that is in him and blind to the liberty of service.” **The dark magician of the legend is the least free figure on his own card.** The one who holds is held.

In passing, Waite praises the deck of Papus, where this card shows not demons but a man and a woman “yoked only to each other”. A chain needs no third party: the bond between two can itself become the chain.

report.h3: Loved for a reflection — and reflections break

report: The circle starts with instinct. A person with 18-6-15 reads a room in a second, sees what someone is missing — and becomes it. For Waite the Moon is “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”, and the way is lit by “only reflected light”. The other falls in love with the reflection, not the person. The light falls both ways: whoever charms easily is just as easily charmed.

Wen writes of the Lovers: “a strong feeling of paradise, at least in the beginning” — but “under every flower a serpent coiled”. In a moonlit union both chose an image, and the person with this tail suspects as much. So the union has to be guarded rather than lived. Where fear of loss lives, chains appear: control, jealousy over things imagined, help with a hook, rescue nobody asked for.

A woman of twenty-four meets a man, and within an hour she knows what he is missing: being understood. She gives him that. Six months later she knows his schedule, has rewritten his CV and lent him money for a course. When he plans a weekend away with friends, she forbids nothing. She just gets sad, and he stays. One day he says he lives under a glass dome with her. She answers that she did everything for him. **That is true — and that is the chain.**

The same tail may be his — the one who stays while suffocating, because “nobody has ever understood me like this”. The Enchanter holds: “he’ll be lost without me”. The Captive clings: “I can’t leave”. And there is a third, the Renouncer: “I don’t need anyone” — a chain put on oneself and called principles. These are not three people but three places on one card.

report.h3: Desire with wings, desire in chains

report: Everyone with this tail has the Empress at the centre of the chart — the comfort zone: being liked, caring, giving gifts. Waite has a line the whole tail rests on: the Empress has been correctly described as “desire and the wings thereof”. Of the Devil he writes: “the chain and fatality of the material life”. We read this as one force described twice: at the centre, desire with wings; at the root, desire in chains.

Hence two kinds of magic. The Empress makes things grow: a gardener never pulls a shoot upwards but gives it water and light, and the harvest leaves the garden — that is what it is for. The Devil holds on: so that it stays, so that it is mine. Giving feels good, but those who receive might leave — and the gift turns into a hook. A present that makes refusal impossible. Help that makes leaving impossible.

Goethe showed this most precisely (the parallel is ours, not the method’s). Faust loves Gretchen but acts through Mephistopheles, who slips her a box of jewels. Gretchen tries on a piece: “How would this chain suit me?” In German, Kette means both a necklace and a chain that binds.

Our reading from here: in this tail two roads lead to the Lovers. The first is the Devil plus the Moon (15 + 18 = 33 → 6): a love born of spells that must then be held on to. The scenario takes this one. The second is the Empress plus the Empress (3 + 3 = 6): two gardens, love from fullness, where neither needs to hold the other. The tail’s whole task is to **reach the same Lovers by the second road**.

report.h3: Influence that survives exposure

report: One question separates a gift from a spell: would the technique still work if the person found out? Influence that survives exposure is mastery; in Waite’s list for the Magician it is “skill, diplomacy, address”. Influence that needs secrecy is a spell. The practices below are the author’s, not a ritual or a promise of results:

ul: say out loud why: texting first “because I missed him” is fine, going silent “so that he’ll miss me” is already a spell;
give only what would still be given if the person left tomorrow — otherwise it is a Kette;
help only when invited: help nobody asked for is the most polite kind of control;
leave night-time decisions until morning: the Moon is strongest in the dark.

report: If something holds so tightly that stopping is impossible, or a relationship involves threats and violence, it takes a professional — a psychotherapist, an addiction specialist, a support group — not a matrix reading.

report.h3: The magician who opens the door

report: A worked-through 18-6-15 is someone next to whom people want to be better — and are still free to leave. The charm stays but works in the open, and the generosity sends no bill. They know the chain from the inside and see better than most where there is love and where a hook. Their magic is measured not by how many people depend on them but by how many grew alongside them and were able to leave.

Waite left this tail a key in a single phrase: the one above the chained pair is “blind to the liberty of service”. Strength that serves someone else’s freedom is the only power that leaves no chains behind. **The Dark Magician holds on. A worked-through 18-6-15 can still enchant, but afterwards opens the door.** And people come back of their own accord.

items.title: Karmic tail 18-6-6 in the destiny matrix: love magic, waiting and love in daylight

seo.title: Karmic tail 18-6-6, “Love Magic”: meaning in the destiny matrix
seo.description: 18-6-6 is the tail where love begins with a reflection. A ten-second date check, why everyone has the Hanged Man at the centre, and what “love magic” really means.

items.short: 18-6-6 is the karmic tail that popular destiny matrix readings call “Love Magic” (less often, “Unrequited Love”). Its scenario: a person falls in love before they have had a chance to see the other person properly — with an image, a promise, a couple of lucky coincidences. And then they hold on to that image with all their might: guessing, waiting, checking, making a living person fit the picture. The Moon (18) opens the circle — imagination shining with reflected light. The Lovers (6), seen by moonlight, keep the circle going: love for a reflection, and a choice that keeps being put off. At the root are the Lovers (6) again, but with a different task — love for a living person seen without veils, and a choice you take responsibility for yourself. So the tail’s main question is not “how do I cast a love spell” or “how do I lift one”, but how to tell a person from their reflection. And everyone with 18-6-6 also has a hidden fourth card — the Hanged Man at the centre of the matrix. More on it below.

sections.h2: Do you have the 18-6-6 tail? A ten-second check
paragraphs: The tail depends entirely on one number: the sum of the first three arcana of the matrix. So you can find 18-6-6 without a calculator.

ol: **Day arcanum** — your day of birth. If it is greater than 22, add its digits: 25 → 7, 31 → 4.
**Month** — its number, from 1 to 12.
**Year arcanum** — the sum of the digits of the year. If it comes out above 22, add the digits again: 1985 → 23 → 5, while 1983 → 21.

paragraphs: Add the three numbers. If you get **33, 42 or 51**, you have 18-6-6. There is also a fourth, rare option — a sum of 6. But only thirteen dates from 1900 to 2100 get it, and all of them fall between January and March (for example, 1 January 2020).

ul: 11.07.1995: 11 + 7 + 6 = 24 → not this one. It is 9-15-6: the same six at the root, but a different tail.
03.10.2000: 3 + 10 + 2 = 15 → not this one. It is 18-6-15: the same entry, the same middle, but the Devil at the root.

paragraphs: Why this works. The sum 33 puts D = 3 + 3 = 6 in the bottom corner of the chart. The centre E = 33 + 6 = 39 → 12. The tail’s entry M = D + E = 6 + 12 = 18, the middle N = D + M = 6 + 18 = 24 → 6. The same happens with the sums 42 and 51: the digits again give 6, and the centre is again 12. There is no other way to 18-6-6 — this was checked by going through every day from 1900 to 2100.
Sums whose digits add up to 6 give three neighbouring tails. People often mix them up:
The same arithmetic yields facts you will rarely find anywhere else:

ul: **It is one of the common tails.** Among birth dates from 1940 to 2012, 18-6-6 comes up on about one in sixteen (6.3%). That is seventh place out of 26 possible tails.

**It is getting older.** Among people born in the 1950s, about one in 13 has it; in the 1990s, one in 17; in the 2000s, only one in 35; and among those born since 2020, one in 40. The reason is arithmetic: it needs a large sum, from 33 up. Years of the 20th century have a large arcanum (1983 → 21), so the day and month only have a little to add. Years of the 2000s have a small arcanum (2004 → 6), and only rare day-and-month combinations reach 33.

**Neighbouring years differ almost sixfold.** In 1983 and 1984, 18-6-6 falls on forty dates — almost one baby in nine. In 1985, on only seven. The most “bumper” years from 1930 to 2030: 1938, 1939, 1947, 1948, 1956, 1957, 1965, 1966, 1974, 1975, 1983, 1984, 1992 and 1993. Their arcanum is 21 or 22, and these are exactly the years in which the 3-7-22 tail never occurs at all. And from 1900 to 2100 there is not a single year in which 18-6-6 falls on nobody.

**6-6-18 is the same tail.** If you see 6, 6 and 18 on the bottom ray of your chart, you are reading the same tail from the outer corner towards the centre. The roles don’t change: the Moon is the entry, the corner six is the root. There is no separate 6-6-18 tail: 18 in the bottom corner only comes from a sum of 18, which gives centre 9 and the tail 9-9-18.

sections.h2: Why “love magic”: in this tail, love comes in through the Moon
paragraphs: Popular interpretations explain the name with a past-life legend. The soul supposedly loved without being loved back and, tired of waiting, turned to a love spell — cast by itself or through someone else — that is, it won love against another person’s will. In other versions it cast love spells for others, was itself their victim, or “used its beauty for harm”. And in this life, the story goes, the person gets too little love — from childhood, from their parents — and spends their whole life looking for it. None of this can be checked; the numbers say nothing about past events. But as a metaphor the legend is precise. This is how someone lives for whom love is something to be **won**, not something that can simply happen between two people.

The word “magic” in the name is no accident. In the popular matrix tradition, magic almost always means the Moon. In the most widespread list of names, five of the 26 tails speak of magic and sorcery — 18-6-6 “Love Magic”, 18-6-15 “the Dark Magician”, 18-9-9 “the Wizard”, 9-9-18 “Magical Knowledge”, 9-18-9 “the Magical Sacrifice” — and all five contain 18. This link also has support in books on the tarot. In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings for the Moon there are “occult forces”, and Benebell Wen calls the Moon the signifier for society’s “magi, priest, or shaman”.

The word “love” is explained by arithmetic. Point M, the entry of the tail, is shared in the method with the relationship line M–R1–R. So everyone with 18-6-6 also has a relationship line that begins with the Moon. And about one in seven — those born in 1938, 1947, 1956, 1965, 1974, 1983, 1992, 2001, 2010 and 2019 — has a relationship line that repeats the very same three numbers. In the tail itself, the Moon is followed by the Lovers twice.

There is also a detail that is hardly ever mentioned. The history of the Lovers card itself once had its own “love magic”. Waite describes how the card looked in 18th-century decks: a pagan Cupid hovers over the pair, flying his shaft. In his own deck Waite replaced this scene and explained why: Cupid is “a misapplied emblem”, the sign “of love beginning rather than of love in its fulness”. Waite knew nothing about the destiny matrix, and this is no proof of the name. But one sentence of his holds the tail’s whole path: from an arrow that strikes without asking to love in its fulness.

sections.h2: Reflected light: how the circle works
paragraphs: This tail has a property you can see right in the calculation. The middle six comes from the root six and the Moon: 6 + 18 = 24, and 2 + 4 = 6. In the matrix’s arithmetic, adding the Moon to a six is like looking at the six in water: the number doesn’t change, only the lighting does. (18 behaves this way with any number from 5 to 11.) There are only two “mirror” tails among the 26, where the middle equals the root — 18-6-6 and 18-9-9 — and both begin with the Moon.

What follows is our reading, not a rule of the method: the middle six is the root six seen by moonlight. The love is the same, but in the mechanism of the scenario the person deals with its reflection, and at the root, with love itself. Conveniently, the six really does look different in the two main tarot authors. For Wen, the Lovers is above all a card of choice, doubt and “an underlying theme of indecision”. Waite, on the other hand, rejects the old picture of a “man between vice and virtue” and calls VI “in all simplicity the card of human love”. The tail’s middle six is closer to the first reading, the root six to the second.

**1. Entry: the Moon draws a person before they have appeared.** Waite writes that the Moon is “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”, and that the dog and the wolf beneath it are “the fears of the natural mind” when there is “only reflected light” to guide it. This is how love begins for 18-6-6. Nothing has happened yet: three meetings, one long look, messages until two in the morning. But inside, a whole person is already complete — with a character, a past and a shared future. The less you know, the more room there is for the image, and the light in which you see your chosen one is reflected: it is the light of your own hopes and fears. Wen adds two precise details. On the card, “the tame side and the wild side are at odds”: a person needs reliability (the dog) and at the same time something wild that takes their breath away (the wolf). And the crayfish crawling out of the water, she says, betrays an unconscious inclination “to take from emotional leftovers”, to scavenge. People with 18-6-6 know this well: for a long time crumbs are enough for them — a rare message, a moment of tenderness, a promise of “later”.

**2. Mechanism: the Lovers by moonlight hold on to the image.** Of the six, Wen writes: “a strong feeling of paradise, at least in the beginning”. And at once she warns that not all is as it seems, and that under every flower there is “a serpent coiled”. Paradise ends when the living person stops matching the reflection. That is when what popular readings call love magic begins — only without candles. The person bends reality to fit the picture: guesses what the other “really meant”, reads signs, tests feelings, holds back so that the other will miss them, lays out the cards on “what he thinks of me”. Or they bend themselves to fit the picture — become the one they think ought to be loved. According to Wen, the male figure on the card is the mind and the female figure is the heart, and in the six they may fail to agree. That is exactly what happens here: the heart chose the image long ago, the mind collects evidence, and the choice of a living person never comes. The mechanism is strong because it gives real highs. Psychology knows this effect well: warmth that comes unpredictably binds more strongly than steady warmth. When affection comes sometimes at once and sometimes a week later, you wait for each instance all the more.

**3. Root: the Lovers in daylight.** In Waite, the man and woman on card VI stand “unveiled before each other”, like Adam and Eve in the first days of paradise. This is love before it is “contaminated by gross material desire”. The root task of the tail is exactly this kind of love: to see the other without veils, with all their flaws, and to stand there yourself without a role, without an “ideal self”. And the second thing at the root is choice. If a love spell is love against another person’s will, then its opposite is love that respects the other’s “no”. It rests not on the other person being unable to leave, but on their being able to — and staying.

**4. Repetition.** Sooner or later the reflection shatters against the living person: “he turned out to be someone else entirely”. And the person with 18-6-6 goes back to their comfort zone — suspended waiting. They can wait for the old image to return: “he’ll change”, “it’s only temporary”. Or they can wait for a new person on whom the same light will fall. Either way the circle starts again, and again with the Moon.

paragraphs: Many people with 18-6-6 recognise all three modes in themselves — in different years. First enchantment and a long wait. After getting burned — armour: work, creativity, “never again”. Then a new meeting, and, so as not to get burned again — sorcery: control, tests, tactics. The sorcery here comes not from malice but from fear. Wen writes of the Moon that a profound vulnerability hides behind the tough shell, and all three modes protect it, each in its own way. From outside it looks like three different people. In fact it is one bottom ray of the chart in different light.

sections.h2: The hidden fourth card: everyone with 18-6-6 has the Hanged Man at the centre
paragraphs: Everyone with the 18-6-6 tail has 12, the Hanged Man, at the centre of the matrix. This is not a coincidence but arithmetic: the centre is always 12, and the tail’s entry is derived from it: M = 6 + 12 = 18. In other words, this tail’s Moon is made of the Lovers and the Hanged Man. Love suspended in waiting becomes a moonlit fog. In the method, the centre of the chart is the comfort zone, the state a person returns to when nobody asks anything of them.

For 18-6-6 an unexpected thing follows: waiting is **comfortable** for them. “Neither yes nor no”, “it’s not clear yet”, “we’ll see” — this is not only torment but also a familiar home. Waite describes the Hanged Man’s face like this: it expresses “deep entrancement, not suffering”. Entrancement is exactly the word. The main “magic” of this tail lives not in love spells but at the centre of the chart: in the calm trance of waiting that you don’t want to leave, because inside it everything is still possible.

But the Hanged Man at the centre is not only a trap; it is also the key. Waite insists that what we see is “life in suspension, but life and not death”, and that it has been called a card of martyrdom and duty “falsely”. So the way out is not to endure longer. Wen sees in the Hanged Man someone who looks at the same things as everyone else, “but through a different perspective”, and asks a question like the Fool’s: will he fall or fly? In the tau cross formed by his legs she sees “the balance between dominion and slavery”. For a tail about love magic, nothing could be more precise: power over someone else’s will and slavery to your own passion are two sides of the same love spell. And among Waite’s divinatory meanings for the Hanged Man are “wisdom, circumspection, discernment”. Discernment is exactly what the Moon lacks.

What follows is our conclusion, not a quotation. The Hanged Man hangs upside down, like a reflection in water, but unlike a reflection, he sees. The task of 18-6-6 is not to break off the waiting by force, but to turn the trance into a vantage point: to use the pause to see what is really going on. Such a pause has a deadline and a question; a trance has neither. Waite writes that whoever understands this card will receive intimations of “a great awakening”. For this tail, awakening looks simple: a person wakes up next to a living person, not next to an image.

sections.h2: How 18-6-6 shows up in life
paragraphs: The scenes below are made-up examples, not a description of everyone with this tail.
Most often people recognise the tail by three plots.

**Falling for an image.** After the second date it is already clear how you will live, where you will go in summer and how he will get on with your mum. Six months later it turns out that he doesn’t like travelling and will never get on with your mum. The weak version of the tail will say: “he’s changed”. The strong one: “he was always like this; I was the one who filled in the picture”.

**A relationship on hold.** “It’s complicated” lasts for years. The other person is only half available: married, in another city, “not ready”, “let’s not rush things”. One message a week is enough to keep going. Picture a woman who forwards his “ok” to three friends, and together they decide whether it is cold or he is just tired. This is Wen’s crayfish feeding on leftovers, and the Hanged Man who hangs there because it is more familiar than falling or flying.

**Sorcery without candles.** Not texting first, so he’ll miss you. Making him jealous. Checking his phone. Using a “technique” from a course on how to keep a man. Laying out the cards on someone else’s feelings or checking compatibility by birth dates. All of this is the same love spell in modern packaging: an attempt to get a feeling while going around a direct conversation. The test is simple: would the trick still work if the other person knew what you were doing? If not, it is not a request but magic.

The strong version in all three plots is the same — daylight. Ask instead of guessing. Name what you want and stay standing through the answer. Tell “he loves me” apart from “I need him”. This tail is not about love being impossible. It is about love being possible only with a real person.

Here the Moon has a real gift. Wen says the card represents “poetry and mystery”, and in Waite moonlight is the light of the imagination. People with 18-6-6 know how to create images that others believe in: in design, photography, film, advertising, on stage, in work with brands and with people. Popular readings often advise them to go into creative professions, and within the tail’s logic this makes sense. Professional “magic” is exactly the ability to show someone what they have not yet seen.

The trap is the same as in love; only the object changes. On the six in work matters, Wen writes plainly: it is a partnership the Seeker is initially excited about, a sense that the match is “made in heaven” — but “not all is as it seems”. You can fall in love with an employer, a project, a business partner. Picture a designer who works for six months on the promise “after the launch we’ll make you a partner”. There is no contract, no figures, no deadlines — just an atmosphere and a shared dream. Then the project closes, or someone else becomes the partner. It is the same scenario: an image instead of terms, waiting instead of choosing, crumbs instead of pay. The same goes for the habit of underpricing yourself to be liked, and for money decisions made on an impression of a person.

The way out is the same too — daylight. Terms on paper, sums in figures, deadlines as dates. Not because people can’t be trusted, but because the Moon of this tail fills in everything that hasn’t been agreed.

Popular readings often say that people with 18-6-6 got too little warmth in childhood: their parents were there but busy, cold or unpredictable, and love had to be guessed at and earned. The numbers know nothing about your childhood. But if this rings true, the link is easy to see. A child who guesses an adult’s mood every evening from the footsteps in the hallway learns early to read signs. That is how lunar sensitivity is born — out of necessity. And as an adult, that person keeps guessing where they could simply ask.

A parent with this tail should look at two things. Do they love an image of the child instead of the child: “he’s going to be a musician”, “she takes after me completely”? And have they made the child the main source of love in their life — the one who has to make up for what they themselves never got? The honest question here is this: what is your child really interested in right now — and do you know that from the child, or from your idea of them?

sections.h2: Love or enchantment: how to tell them apart
paragraphs: **Person or reflection:**

ul: Can you name three flaws of this person without adding “but on the other hand”?
What do you know about them from their actions, and what from guesses about their feelings?
Where are your feelings stronger — when you meet, or in the pauses between meetings? If in the pauses, what holds you is not the person but the waiting.
If tomorrow they gave you a clear “no”, what would you lose: a person you know, or a future you invented?

paragraphs: **Request or love spell:**

ul: Would your trick still work if the other person found out about it? A trick that only works in secret is a love spell, even without candles and incantations.
Do you leave the other person the right to refuse without being punished — without coldness, resentment, revenge?
Do you ask for what you need, or arrange things so that the other person “works it out on their own”?
Does your waiting have an object and a deadline: what exactly are you waiting for, and until what date?
Are you waiting for the situation to become clear, or for the other person to change?
What is happening to your life while you wait: are you living it, or keeping it on pause?

sections.h2: What to do with the 18-6-6 tail: seven practices
paragraphs: These are the author’s exercises, drawn from the logic of the triple — not a ritual and not a promise of results.

ol: **A record instead of guesswork.** When you badly want to understand “what this means”, divide a sheet of paper into three columns. In the first, write what the person literally did or said, as in an official record. In the second, what you felt. In the third, what you added in your head. Decisions are made from the first column only. The Moon does not fall silent because of this, but it stops passing off a reflection as fact.

**Don’t guess at what you can ask.** Before laying out the cards, calculating compatibility or gathering advice from friends, put the question to the person themselves. One direct question is worth ten spreads. The tail forbids nothing, but guessing at someone else’s feelings feeds exactly the part of the scenario you want to get out of.

**A deadline for waiting.** The Hanged Man at the centre makes a pause comfortable, so the pause needs a date: “I’ll wait for a clear answer until the first of November; after that, I decide.” A pause with a deadline is a vantage point. A pause without one is a trance.

**Bread, not crumbs.** Once a month, write down what you actually get in the relationship: how much time, what actions, what words. Next to it, write what you need. If the gap is big, you are living on leftovers, like Wen’s crayfish. Say so out loud — first to yourself, then to the other person.

**A request instead of a trick.** Turn every “tactic” into a request. Not “I won’t text, let him miss me” but “it matters to me that you sometimes text first”. A request is more honest and, oddly enough, works more often: it can be answered.

**Several sources of warmth.** Popular readings speak of a “hunger for tenderness” in people with this tail. If this is you, don’t make one person your only source of warmth. Friends, family, hugs, dancing, sport, massage, your own creative work — when warmth comes from several places, a pause in a relationship stops feeling like hunger, and it becomes easier to see clearly.

**Choose in daylight.** The root six is a choice with a price. When you choose, name out loud what you are giving up: other options, “what if he still changes”, the future you invented. And don’t make important decisions about love at night, on a wave of feeling. The Moon is strongest in the dark, and a decision that has survived the morning is usually a real one.

sections.h2: The strength of 18-6-6: seeing in the dark and loving in the light
paragraphs: In its worked-through version this tail gives a rare combination. The person senses shades finely and notices what others miss (the Moon). They know how to love deeply (the Lovers). They can bear uncertainty without destroying themselves or anyone else (the Hanged Man). They know the fog from the inside, and so they see better than others where a friend has not love but an obsession. People come to them to “break the spell” — not with a ritual but with a sober conversation. Wen links the Hanged Man with the archetype of the wounded healer, who helps others precisely because they were wounded themselves.

Imagination doesn’t go anywhere — and it shouldn’t. Wen makes a subtle observation about the Moon card: the first clarity may come “from the moon, the reflection, rather than from the sun itself”. An image is not an enemy but the first light. Trouble begins only when it is taken for the last.

Waite ends his description of the Moon with the words that calm the storm in the Gospels: “Peace, be still.” And he adds that perhaps then a calm will come upon the animal nature. Right after the Moon in the deck comes the Sun — for Waite, “the direct as the antithesis of the reflected light”. A worked-through 18-6-6 is love that can stand direct light.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: **Calculation** — the classic destiny matrix scheme with points A–T: D = A + B + C, E = A + B + C + D, M = D + E, N = D + M; every sum over 22 is reduced by adding its digits. All numerical facts in the article — the sums 33, 42, 51 and 6, the constant centre 12, frequencies by year and generation, the match with the relationship line — come from going through every date from 1900 to 2100.
**Card meanings** — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, reissued 1922) and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Quotations are given in the authors’ original English.

**The name “Love Magic” and the past-life legend** come from popular interpretations of the destiny matrix. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the matrix or karmic tails: putting the three cards together into a scenario, reading the middle six as a reflection of the root six and the centre as the key are the author’s interpretation.

This is an esoteric model for self-observation, not a forecast and not a substitute for help from a psychologist. If a relationship involves threats, violence or coercion, the cause is neither the tail nor you: what is needed here is real help, not work with numbers.

sections.h2: This tail in compatibility
paragraphs: For a couple, 18-6-6 can be read as the task of choosing each other without requiring feelings to be guessed. The Moon at M concerns shared wishes that can remain hints; the Lovers at N develop the task through practical choices about closeness; the Lovers at D return the focus to accepting a real person and respecting oneself within the relationship. The sixes have different roles rather than “doubling love.” This connection is our reading of Lisovskaya’s pair positions, not a ready-made description from her book.

Both people may want a special weekend, while one hopes for a surprise and the other thinks the best gift is an unplanned day. By evening, one shared wish for time together can produce two disappointments. The Moon makes a lovely day easy to imagine, but the middle six asks the couple to choose its form together. The six in the central task matters when mismatched expectations are about to become a judgement of the partner: “Someone who loved me would have known.”

Before the weekend, each name one wish and one constraint, then make a plan you both actually accept. Afterwards, discuss what you enjoyed without passing judgement on the whole relationship. The difficulty is searching for an option so perfect that every real proposal falls short. A small shared choice that allows for different tastes is useful here: it gives feelings a practical form while letting each person remain themselves.

faq.q: What happened in the past life of a person with the 18-6-6 tail?
faq.a: Popular interpretations speak of unrequited love and a love spell cast by the person themselves, at their request, or for others. Less often — of the person having been the victim of a love spell, having lived in illusions, or having “used their beauty for harm”. This is a legend of the tradition: neither numbers nor cards establish events in past lives. It is more useful to read it as a description of what can already be seen now — the habit of winning love by waiting, cunning or self-denial instead of reaching an agreement about it.

faq.q: Does 18-6-6 mean someone has put a love spell on me, or that I cast love spells myself?
faq.a: No. The tail is three numbers derived from a date of birth. It cannot show whether someone performed a ritual on you or you on someone else, and no “removal” service changes these numbers. People with this tail often feel “as if I’ve been bewitched”, but the scenario itself explains that feeling better: a vivid image, unpredictable warmth and comfortable waiting hold you more tightly than any incantation. Those are what to work on, not an imaginary curse.

faq.q: Can I read cards about love with the 18-6-6 tail?
faq.a: Popular readings often advise keeping away from love spells and love readings. The tail forbids nothing, but the advice has its logic. A spread on “what does he feel for me” gives the Moon new material for the image and puts off the only question that matters — the one you put to the person themselves. Cards, including the ones this article is about, are more useful for a conversation with yourself: what do I feel, what am I afraid of, what am I choosing.

faq.q: Do two sixes mean two loves, or a love triangle?
faq.a: No. A repeated arcanum does not double events and does not predict how many relationships there will be. The two sixes stand in different positions and do different work: the middle one keeps the scenario going — doubt and love for an image; the root one sets the goal — choosing a living person. If a triangle has happened in your life after all, it grew out of the mechanism, out of the attempt not to choose, rather than out of the number.

faq.q: How is 18-6-6 different from 18-6-15?
faq.a: Their entry and middle are the same: the Moon and the Lovers. The root and the centre differ. 18-6-15 (in popular lists, “the Dark Magician”) has the Devil at the root and the Empress at the centre, and it comes from the sum 15. Wen explains the difference between the two cards in a single line: the Lovers is about “one choice”, the Devil is about “being led astray”. In her description of the Devil, the chained figures are the same Lovers. Put simply, 18-6-6 learns to choose, while 18-6-15 learns to free itself from what already holds it.

faq.q: I have 18-6-6 and my relationship line is also 18-6-6 — is that the same thing?
faq.a: This happens for about one holder of this tail in seven: those born in years with the arcanum 21, 3 or 12 (1938, 1947, 1956, 1965, 1974, 1983, 1992, 2001, 2010, 2019). Point M is shared by the tail and the relationship line, so the numbers match. But there are still two triples: the line M–R1–R describes how you build closeness, while the tail M–N–D is a scenario that repeats by itself. The match only means that the same cards are at work in closeness and in the old scenario, and the practices in this article apply to both.

faq.q: Is 18-6-6 different for women and men?
faq.a: No. Gender plays no part in the calculation, and the meaning of the tail doesn’t depend on it. Popular readings like to split it into “the woman looking for a rescuer” and “the man drawn to femmes fatales”, but these are stereotypes, not arithmetic. Anyone can be the Enchanted, the Sorcerer or the Armour — and most often it is one and the same person in different years.

faq.q: Can the 18-6-6 tail be “closed”?
faq.a: The numbers in the matrix don’t change — what changes is how the scenario plays out. Signs of a worked-through tail: you notice when you are filling in a person and ask instead of guessing; your waiting has a deadline; tricks have been replaced by requests; you can hear “no” without falling apart; next to you is a person you see as they are — and you choose them anyway.

faq.q: What if my child has 18-6-6?
faq.a: Give them what this tail looks for all its life: predictable warmth and direct words. Don’t make them guess your mood; name it: “I’m tired, it’s not because of you.” Hug them not only as a reward. Ask what they feel, and don’t argue with the answer. Their imagination is a gift, and it is worth feeding with books, drawing and theatre, but they need an adult nearby who helps them tell what was imagined from what happened. There are fewer such children now than in their parents’ generation: among people born after 2000, about one in 35 has 18-6-6.

People with 18-6-6 can live on crumbs for a long time: a rare message, a moment of tenderness, a promise of “later”.

report.h3: A love spell that needs no candles

report: Of the six, Wen writes: “a strong feeling of paradise, at least in the beginning”. She also warns: “under every flower a serpent coiled”. Paradise ends when the living person stops matching the reflection. Then the love magic begins. Guessing what the other “really meant”. Reading signs. Holding back so as to be missed. Checking the phone, laying out cards on “what he thinks of me”. Or reshaping oneself to fit the picture.

All of this tries to get a feeling while bypassing a direct conversation. The test is simple: a trick that only works in secret is the same love spell. The mechanism holds fast because it gives real highs: warmth that comes unpredictably binds harder than steady warmth.

report.h3: The real spell lives at the centre of the chart

report: Everyone with 18-6-6 has 12, the Hanged Man, at the centre of the matrix. That is arithmetic: the centre is always 12, and the entry is derived from it, 6 + 12 = 18. This tail’s Moon is made of the Lovers and the Hanged Man: love suspended in waiting becomes moonlit fog. In the method, the centre of the chart is the comfort zone, where a person returns when nothing is asked of them.

An unexpected conclusion follows: for this tail, waiting is **comfortable**. “Neither yes nor no”, “it’s not clear yet”, “we’ll see” — not only torment but a familiar home. The Hanged Man’s face, Waite writes, “expresses deep entrancement, not suffering”. Here lives the real magic of 18-6-6: not in a love spell but in the calm trance of waiting, which nobody hurries to leave, because inside it everything is still possible.

But the Hanged Man is not only a trap; it is also the key. For Waite, the figure suggests “life in suspension, but life and not death”, and the card’s divinatory meanings include “wisdom, circumspection, discernment”. Discernment is exactly what the Moon lacks. In the Hanged Man’s pose Wen sees “the balance between dominion and slavery”. For love magic, nothing could be more precise: power over another’s will and slavery to one’s own passion are two sides of the same spell.

What follows is our conclusion, not a quotation. The Hanged Man hangs upside down, like a reflection in water, but unlike a reflection, he sees. The task is not to break off the waiting by force but to turn the trance into a vantage point. Such a pause has a deadline and a question; a trance has neither.

report.h3: The opposite of a love spell is the freedom to leave

report: At the root are the Lovers again, but in daylight. On Waite’s card VI the man and woman stand “unveiled before each other”, like Adam and Eve in the first days of paradise. The root task is to see the other without veils and to stand there without a role. And to choose. If a love spell is love against another’s will, its opposite respects the other’s “no”. **It rests not on the other being unable to leave, but on their being able to — and staying.**
Simple things change the scenario:

ul: ask instead of guessing: one direct question is worth ten spreads;
give the waiting a deadline: “I’ll wait for a clear answer until the first of November; after that, I decide”;
turn a trick into a request: not “I won’t text, let him miss me” but “it matters to me to get the first message sometimes”;
make no decisions about love at night, on a wave of feeling: a decision that survives the morning is usually real.

report: The tail is a model for self-observation, not a substitute for a psychologist. If a relationship involves threats, violence or coercion, the tail is not the cause: what is needed is real help, not work with numbers.

Worked through, 18-6-6 gives a person who senses fine shades, can love deeply and can bear uncertainty. Such a person knows the fog from the inside and sees better than most where a friend has not love but an obsession. People come to them to “break the spell” — not with a ritual but with a sober conversation.

Wen observes that the first clarity may come “from the moon, the reflection, rather than from the sun itself”. **An image is not an enemy but the first light.** Trouble begins when it is taken for the last. Waite ends his account of the Moon with the words that calm the storm in the Gospels: “Peace, be still.” Right after the Moon comes the Sun — “the direct as the antithesis of the reflected light”. **A worked-through 18-6-6 is love that can stand direct light.**

items.title: Karmic tail 18-9-9 in the destiny matrix: “Forbidden Knowledge”, moonlight and a lantern under the cloak

seo.title: Karmic tail 18-9-9 “Forbidden Knowledge” in the destiny matrix
seo.description: 18-9-9 is the tail of someone who sees more than others but keeps the lantern under the cloak. A one-minute date check, three Hermits and how to raise the light.

items.short: 18-9-9 is the karmic tail that popular destiny matrix guides call “Forbidden Knowledge” (less often “Magical Knowledge”, “The Mage” or “The Hermit”). Its script goes like this. In an unclear situation the person notices more than others, but sees it by reflected light and fills in the picture at once: that is the entry, the Moon (18). They carry their version off into silence, where nobody can check it: that is the mechanism, the Hermit (9). The root task is also the Hermit, but with a different lantern: to bring what they have understood back to people and raise the light so that others can use it. In a word — don’t keep the lantern under your cloak. This is one of the most common tails: fourth of the 26, roughly one birth date in eleven since 1900. And everyone who has it shares one more card, a third Hermit — more on that below.

sections.h2: Do you have the 18-9-9 tail: a one-minute check
paragraphs: You can find 18-9-9 without a calculator. It comes up if, and only if, the sum of the first three numbers of the matrix is divisible by 9 and is at least 27 — that is, it equals **27, 36, 45 or 54**.

ol: **Day arcanum** — the day you were born. If it is over 22, add its digits: 25 → 7, 29 → 11, 31 → 4.
**Month** — its number, from 1 to 12.
**Year arcanum** — the sum of the digits of the year. If it comes out over 22, add the digits again: 1995 → 24 → 6, 1989 → 27 → 9, while 2007 → 9.

paragraphs: Add the three numbers.

ul: 22.03.1986: 22 + 3 + 6 = 31 → not this one (this date has the tail 12-16-4).

paragraphs: The two other sums that are multiples of nine give mirror images of this set. Exactly **18** gives the tail 9-9-18 (for example 05.04.1989: 5 + 4 + 9). Exactly **9** gives the tail 9-18-9 (01.06.2000: 1 + 6 + 2). The numbers are the same, but the tails are different, and the difference is not a formality: more on it in the questions section.

Why this works. The bottom corner of the chart, D, is the reduced sum of the three numbers: 27, 36, 45 and 54 all reduce to 9. The centre E is the same sum plus D: that gives 36, 45, 54 or 63, which is 9 again. After that there is no choice: the entry M = D + E = 9 + 9 = 18, the middle N = D + M = 9 + 18 = 27 → 9. There are no other routes to 18-9-9 — this was checked by running every day from 1900 to 2100.
The same arithmetic leads to a few facts that are rarely written about:

ul: **It is not rare.** 18-9-9 accounts for 8.9% of birth dates from 1900 to 2025 — fourth place out of the 26 possible tails. Among people born in the 20th century it is roughly every tenth day; among those born from 2000 to 2025, every seventeenth, but even there the tail keeps fourth place. The reason is arithmetic: the years of the 2000s have a small year arcanum, so it is harder for the day and month to bring the sum up to 27.
**The mirrors are much rarer.** 9-9-18 is about one date in 50. 9-18-9 is one in 470, next to last of the 26.
**There are “rich” years.** The tail comes up most often in years with arcanum 22: 1939, 1948, 1957, 1966, 1975, 1984, 1993 — 42 days in each. Least often in 2000: just 11 days.
**December beats January.** Among people born in December 10.7% have 18-9-9, in January 6.8%. The month number goes into the sum, and a December date reaches 27 more easily.

sections.h2: Where the name “Forbidden Knowledge” comes from
paragraphs: Popular interpretations explain the name with a past-life legend. The soul supposedly possessed secret knowledge — it was a mage, a priest, a village healer, a scholar in seclusion — and used it badly. Some versions speak of black magic, love spells and power over other people’s minds through fear. Others tell of a person who withdrew from people and took the knowledge with them, passing it on to nobody. This cannot be checked: a birth date tells nothing about events in the past. But the name has a footing in the cards themselves, and examining that footing leads to an unexpected turn.

The first footing is in the Moon. Benebell Wen calls it the signifier of “society’s magi, priest, or shaman”. For her the High Priestess holds esoteric knowledge, and the Moon is **“the beginning manifestation into consciousness of that esoteric knowledge”**: what rises from the depths and has not yet become clear. The second footing is in the Hermit. As far back as 1910 Waite was retelling interpretations in which the Hermit’s lantern holds “the Light of Occult Science” and his staff is “a Magic Wand”. His own answer was that such readings are “true after their own manner”, but miss all the high things for which the Major Arcana exist.

And here is the turn. Waite argues separately against the most widespread understanding of this card — as a symbol of **“occult isolation”**, the protection of “personal magnetism” against admixture. He calls it one of the frivolous renderings inherited from Éliphas Lévi. Anyone who reads esoteric literature knows the modern retelling of this idea: “protect your energy”, “don’t let people into your field”, “the people around you drain you”. For a person with 18-9-9 this is the most tempting explanation of all, because it justifies their mechanism. Waite objects: the true mysteries **“secure their own protection from those who are unprepared”**. There is no need to hide them.

Hence our reading of the name. In 18-9-9 nobody forbade the knowledge from outside. The person sets the ban themselves — not on knowing, but on showing, checking and giving away. The legend of a mage who took his knowledge to the grave remains a legend. As a metaphor it is exact: this tail is home to someone who knows more than they say.

sections.h2: How the circle works: reflected light, a cloak and a beacon
paragraphs: **1. Entry: the Moon sees more than it lights up.** On Waite’s card a road runs between two towers into the unknown. The dog and the wolf at the edge of the road are “the fears of the natural mind” in the presence of that exit into the unknown, “when there is only reflected light to guide it”. Waite adds that the light of the intellect is a reflection, and beyond it lies a mystery it cannot show. He describes the card itself as “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”.

In life it looks quite ordinary. A reply came back shorter than usual. A meeting was moved without explanation. The boss said hello more drily than yesterday. A person with 18-9-9 notices such things first, and often notices correctly — that is the Moon’s real strength. But by reflected light you can see that something is there, not what it is. An old fear fills the gap. In our reading the dog and the wolf sound like two voices: “you’re not wanted here” and “you’re being used here”. Within a few seconds a version takes shape — whole, convincing, and it feels not like a guess but like knowledge.

**2. Mechanism: the Hermit covers the lantern with his cloak.** Then the person does not ask. They step back to figure it out on their own. Wen offers two readings of the Hermit’s lantern. In the first it is a light shining for others in the dark. In the second it is someone who “sees the world through his or her own light” and walks only where their thoughts lead. The middle nine of this tail is the second version. In silence the version gets no new data, it gets details. The longer the person thinks alone, the more coherent the story invented in the first few seconds looks, and the more dangerous a simple question seems.

Waite’s Moon has one more detail — a creature crawling out of the water. It is a vague movement from the depths that “strives to attain manifestation” and crawls onto the land, “but as a rule it sinks back whence it came”. You could not invent a better image for 18-9-9. The phrase “I felt uneasy, has something happened?” almost reaches the shore — and sinks back into the water. Wen sees a hard shell on this crayfish, with “a profound vulnerability that the Seeker is trying to conceal from others” underneath. Outside — calm and a slight distance; inside — a hurt nobody has seen.

The people around them don’t know they have already been discussed and judged. They meet a polite distance and answer with the same. The coolness that comes back becomes proof of the first version: “I knew it.” The circle confirms itself. The silence produces exactly the estrangement the person was afraid of.

**3. Why the circle is so strong: the Hermit is in the centre too.** Everyone with 18-9-9 has 9 in the centre of the matrix. In the method the centre is the comfort zone, the point a person returns to in order to recover. So withdrawing into yourself does not feel like a problem here. It feels like home, like rest, like the only right decision. The tail is held together not by suffering but by comfort, and that is why it goes unnoticed for so long. The arithmetic says this almost word for word: the Moon of this tail is made of two Hermits, the centre and the root (9 + 9 = 18). Fog is born where solitude meets solitude. It is a play of numbers, not a proof, but an exact one.

**4. Root: the Hermit raises the lantern.** At the root stands the Hermit again, but a different one. Waite stresses that this is a card of **attainment rather than of quest**. His Hermit does not wander in the dark; he stands on a height and holds up a lantern with a star shining in it. Waite conveys the meaning of this beacon in a single phrase: **“where I am, you also may be”**. And one more detail that is easy to miss: unlike the familiar images before him, where the lantern is partly wrapped in the cloak, in Waite it is uncovered.

The task of 18-9-9 is not to stop being a Hermit. With three nines in the chart that is neither possible nor necessary. The task is to change what the lantern does: instead of “I see the world through my own light” — “I give light to others”. To come back from the silence with a result: a question, a conclusion, a decision, a thought said out loud, knowledge passed on. The solitude stays, but now it has a return address.

**5. Repeat.** If the root is not reached, the next unclear situation meets the person with one more “proof” in reserve. With each round the Moon becomes more convincing — because the silence has never once let it be wrong out loud.
**How to tell that the tail has switched on right now:**

ul: you are sure, even though you haven’t asked anything;
the conversation is replaying in your head for the third time, and with the person themselves not once;
you’ve decided to “just step back a little” — silently and with no end date;
you expect the other person to guess on their own;
“I’ll sort it out myself” is said about something that concerns two people.

sections.h2: Two nines, two different lanterns
paragraphs: A repeated arcanum does not mean “double loneliness”. The two nines stand in different roles and do opposite work. Remarkably, both sources know this double nature of the Hermit. Waite contrasts his uncovered lantern with the usual one, hidden under the cloak. Wen gives two readings of the lantern and separately distinguishes the Hermit’s withdrawal from the withdrawal in the Four of Cups: there a person turns inward out of past disappointment and “may be licking wounds”, while the Hermit turns inward to seek enlightenment.

head: The middle 9 (N) — mechanism
The root 9 (D) — task
rows: “I see the world through my own light”
“I shine a light for others in the dark”
to hide from the unclear, to lick wounds
to think and come back with an answer

paragraphs: From the outside they are hard to tell apart: both are silent. The difference is in the direction. The middle Hermit withdraws from people. The root Hermit withdraws in order to come back to them.

sections.h2: The third Hermit and the echo: where else 9 and 18 stand in your chart
paragraphs: The 18-9-9 tail is not a corner of the chart you can walk around. The arithmetic that assembles this tail places the same two arcana all over the matrix. Here is what everyone with it shares, without exception:

head: Where in the matrix
What everyone with 18-9-9 has
rows: Centre of the chart E — comfort zone
Start of the relationship line M–R1–R
18 · The Moon (it is the same point M)
Sky line (month — D — their sum), middle
only 9 or 18, and at least one of them is 18

paragraphs: **Purposes.** The personal, social, spiritual and planetary purposes of people with 18-9-9 can only be the Hermit or the Moon. The arithmetic leaves no other options. Adding digits does not change the remainder after division by 9, and the sum of the first three numbers of this tail is divisible by 9, as is D. Each purpose is ultimately built from the same A, B, C and D, so it is divisible by 9 as well, and between 1 and 22 there are two such numbers: 9 and 18. At least one of the four purposes is always the Moon: if the personal and social purposes are both 9, the spiritual becomes 9 + 9 = 18. The personal purpose is the Hermit for 65% of people with this tail and the Moon for 35%.

For reading the chart this is an important conclusion, though it is ours and not from a book. These people have the Hermit and the Moon both in the “problem” and in the “purpose”. What works as fog and a cloak in the tail becomes the same material in mature form in the purpose: seeing what is hidden and giving light to others. The tail here is not someone else’s load to be thrown off, but a raw version of your own gift.

**Relationships.** The Moon that the tail starts with is the same point M that the relationship line starts with. For 18-9-9 the entry into the script and the entry into closeness coincide. So the main stage of this tail is relationships with people; more on them below.

**A triple coincidence.** If you were born in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 or 2025 and have 18-9-9, the same triad also stands on your relationship line and your money line. For those born in 1980, 1971, 1962, 1953, 1944, 1935, 1926, 1917 and 1908 the relationship line is also 18-9-9, and the money line is 9-18-9. On these lines the triad is no longer a karmic tail but the program of that area of life, and it should be read according to the meaning of the line. But such a chart has one theme, and it sounds louder than usual.

**Age.** On the age scale the bottom corner D falls on the decade from 60 to 70, and everyone with this tail has the Hermit there. Waite’s figure blends “the Ancient of Days” and “the Light of the World”. This is a rhyme of images, not a forecast.

sections.h2: How 18-9-9 shows up in life
paragraphs: The scenes below are made-up examples, not a description of everyone with this tail.
Wen links the watery nature of the Moon with interpersonal relationships, and in the matrix the Moon of this tail literally opens the relationship line. This is where the circle is most visible.

The most recognisable scene is **the test of silence**. Something has hurt, but instead of speaking the person goes quiet and watches to see whether the partner will notice. The partner doesn’t know there is an exam going on, carries on as usual — and fails a test nobody told them about. The lantern is hidden under the cloak, and the other person is supposed to make out in the dark what you are holding. The second scene is **half-presence**: at the table, in the conversation, in the same bed, but inside — in a cell the other person is not allowed into. From the outside it looks like coldness. From the inside it feels like self-care.

Picture this: a partner who usually writes long messages replies “ok”. In a minute the Moon puts together a story: they’re tired of me, they’re hiding something, they’ve started pulling away. The middle Hermit suggests putting the phone down and “not imposing”. In the evening the person is reserved, the partner feels the chill and closes up too — the story is confirmed. The lived-through version of the tail makes a different move, and it does not require feeling less. It takes one sentence: “You’re short with me today. Tired, or has something happened?” The Moon’s observation was right — something really had changed. Only the explanation, invented alone, was wrong.

In the strong version 18-9-9 has a rare talent for closeness. Such a person senses another’s state before any words. They can be there in a heavy silence without running away and without filling the quiet with noise. You can be silent with them — and that is not an empty phrase: it is exactly what many people lack. The only question is whether their own feelings sometimes reach the shore too.

The work circle starts with unclear feedback. The manager didn’t reply to the report, a colleague didn’t invite them to a meeting. The person decides they are in disfavour, stops putting themselves forward, finishes the work alone in the evenings, shows the result late or not at all. They are noticeably less visible, they are trusted less — and that confirms the version again.

The second trap is **the secret workshop**. The person knows their field deeply, but nobody knows that they know. A manuscript in the drawer, a project that is “almost ready”, an idea that is “too early to share”. The inner phrase: “I’ll show it when I’ve worked it all out.” Waite’s thought is especially useful here: the Hermit is a card of attainment, not of quest. The root nine does not demand that you get to the very end. It says you have already come far enough to give light. In this tail money comes to the raised lantern — when knowledge gets a name, a price and an address where it can be found.

Picture an analyst who is the first to spot an error in the quarterly accounts. She doesn’t want to “make a fuss” in case she is the one who got it wrong, and decides to check everything again — silently. Three weeks later the error comes out in front of everyone, and she thinks: “I saw it.” That is the tail: the Moon noticed, the Hermit hid it. The lived-through version sounds modest: “Take a look at line fourteen, I don’t think it adds up.”

Where the Moon and the Hermit together work as a talent: research and analytics, finding hidden errors, editing and translation — anything where the unclear has to be made clear. Also psychology and counselling, literature, music, design, investigation, teaching and mentoring. The specific profession is decided by interests and skills; the cards only give a direction.

A recognisable scene is **the friend who disappears**. “I don’t want to burden anyone” — and then several months of silence. After that coming back feels awkward, and the longer the pause, the more awkward it gets. The Hermit’s beacon works the other way round: nobody knows “where I am”. A short signal with the lantern raised is enough: “I’m in my cave right now, it’s not about you. I’ll tell you about it when I’m back.”

If a child has 18-9-9, it is usually a small person with a rich imagination, night-time fears and a need to be alone for a while. They need a night light — literally and figuratively. Don’t brush the fear aside (“nonsense, go to sleep”) and don’t blow it up; check it together: switch on the light and look in the wardrobe. That is the main practice of the whole tail — looking at the version by direct light, not by reflected light. Respect their solitude, but add a return: “Have some time alone, and then tell me what you came up with.” There are quite a few such children: among people born since 2000, roughly one in seventeen has 18-9-9.

It is often said that people with 18-9-9 are drawn to tarot, astrology, psychology and esotericism. This is not a given, but it makes sense: for Wen the Moon is the card of the mage and the shaman. If you are drawn to it, this tail has one test: does the practice bring you to people and facts, or replace them? Waite warns plainly about the Moon’s main trap: it is the life of the imagination, not of the spirit. The main risk is mistaking imagination for revelation. An insight that frightens (“a curse”, “enemies”, “someone has put the evil eye on you”) is the Moon under the cloak. An insight that clarifies is the Hermit’s lantern. A practitioner with this tail who keeps knowledge “for the chosen few” is doing exactly what Waite objected to: turning a mystery into isolation.

sections.h2: Intuition or guesswork, solitude or isolation
paragraphs: The whole 18-9-9 tail rests on four substitutions. Learn to tell them apart, and the circle loses half its power.

**Intuition or guesswork.** Intuition starts with a specific observation and is not afraid of being checked. Guesswork starts with a ready-made story and avoids checking. A simple test: can you name what exactly you saw or heard — without the words “clearly”, “obviously”, “I can just feel it”?

**Solitude or isolation.** Solitude has a time limit and a result: the person went away to think and came back with a thought. Isolation has neither a time limit nor a result. Wen separates them through the Hermit and the Four of Cups: withdrawing to seek light — or to lick your wounds.

**Mystery or secrecy.** A mystery is something you treasure because it is yours. Secrecy is something you hide because you fear the consequences of talking about it. According to Waite, the true mysteries protect themselves. If something has to be guarded, what is being guarded is usually not knowledge but fear.

**A quiet mind or punishing silence.** A quiet mind calms the agitation. In Waite it is the “calm gaze” that the face of the mind directs upon the unrest below. Punishing silence stores up the agitation and passes it on to the other person: “work out for yourself what you did.”

sections.h2: The tail in shadow and in light
paragraphs: The phrases “the tail in minus” and “the tail in plus” are easier to understand as two ways of handling the same material, not as a property of a person.

sections.h2: What to do with the 18-9-9 tail: eight practices
paragraphs: These are the author’s own exercises, drawn from the logic of the triad — not a ritual and not a guarantee of results.

ol: **Two columns.** When a version switches on, divide a sheet of paper in half. On the left, only what you saw and heard: facts, quotes, times. On the right, what you concluded from it. The Moon lives in the gap between the columns. If the right column is three times longer than the left, you are looking by reflected light.

**Three explanations, one of them boring.** Before acting on a version, come up with two more explanations of the same fact, and make one of them deliberately boring: “they were tired”, “they didn’t see the message”, “they were on the underground”. The goal is not to talk yourself into believing everything is fine, but to give the uncertainty back its real size.

**A pause with a return address.** When you step away to think, name a time: “I need to think, I’ll come back to this tomorrow evening.” Solitude with a time limit is the Hermit. Solitude without one is the cloak.

**One question into the light.** The smallest check is one neutral sentence: “I noticed that… Does it mean something, or did I imagine it?” Ask it within a day. The longer a version lives in the dark, the stronger it gets.

**Let the crayfish onto the shore.** Once a week, say one of the sentences that usually stay with you: “I was hurt”, “I missed you”, “I don’t agree with this”. Even if it is awkward, even if it is bad timing. Waite’s creature “as a rule sinks back” — your task is to break that rule at least once.

**The lantern on the table.** Show someone one unfinished thing: a draft, a sketch, a half-formed idea. Explain what you know to someone who knows less. The root Hermit is a card of attainment: you already have something to shine with.

**Someone else’s lantern.** On a question you are used to solving alone, ask the advice of someone more experienced. In Wen the Hermit is both the one who gives light to others and the one who should accept the counsel of someone wiser. The blind spot of this tail is the belief that only your own lantern can give light.

**“Peace, be still.”** Waite ends his description of the Moon with the Gospel words that calm the storm. For him peace comes not from running away but from a calm gaze at the water. When fear rises, give yourself ten minutes of doing nothing: don’t write, don’t leave, don’t argue with yourself. Just name what has surfaced: “this is the fear that I’m not wanted”. A named fear becomes a question; an unnamed one becomes a version of events.

paragraphs: The signs that the practice is working are modest and easy to check. You ask before you have had time to feel hurt. The people close to you know when you have gone off to think and when you will be back. Drafts come out of the drawer. Your versions turn out to be wrong more and more often — and that is good news: it means they are finally being checked.

sections.h2: The strong side: a person who is not afraid of the dark
paragraphs: In its lived-through version 18-9-9 gives a rare combination. The Moon lets you see what is hidden from others: subtext, atmosphere, a faint signal, the error on line fourteen. The middle Hermit gives the ability to work long and deep on your own, without needing noise or approval. The root Hermit turns this into light for others. Wen writes that the first clarity comes from the moon, from the reflection, rather than from the sun itself. People with 18-9-9 are often that first clarity: they notice before it gets light.

This is the person people call when it is dark. They are not frightened by someone else’s anxiety, because they know it from the inside. They are in no hurry with consolation, because they know how to be silent. And if they have lived through their tail, they don’t leave another person alone in the fog — they raise the lantern. Someone who once stood by a night road with only reflected light, while the dog and the wolf howled, becomes the one who holds a lantern on that road for others.
Waite puts it in a single phrase, and for 18-9-9 it sounds like the formula for the way out: “where I am, you also may be.”

sections.h2: How is 18-9-9 different from 9-9-18 and 9-18-9?
paragraphs: The set of numbers is the same, but the roles and even the centre of the chart are different. It all comes down to the sum of the day arcanum, the month and the year arcanum.

rows: in the mechanism and in the centre
version → withdrawal → come back with a lantern
withdrawal → withdrawal → learn to tell imagination from reality
withdrawal → fog in the silence → bring meaning out

paragraphs: In 18-9-9 the circle is set off by uncertainty, to which the person responds by withdrawing. In 9-18-9 it is the other way round: habitual withdrawal creates a silence in which the fog grows by itself. In 9-9-18 the Moon is not the entry but the root task: learning to pass through uncertainty without taking it for the truth.

sections.h2: What this article is based on

ul: **Calculation** — Natalia Ladini’s classic destiny matrix scheme with points A–T: D = A + B + C, E = A + B + C + D, M = D + E, N = D + M; every sum over 22 is reduced by adding its digits. The “27, 36, 45 or 54” rule was checked by running every day from 1900 to 2100. Frequencies, years, months and the constant points of the chart were counted over all dates from 1900 to 2025.
**Card meanings** — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, 1922 reprint) and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Both are quoted in the original English.

**The name “Forbidden Knowledge” and the past-life legend** are taken from popular interpretations of the destiny matrix. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the matrix or karmic tails. Assembling the three cards into a script, reading the two nines as two lanterns and the centre as the reason the circle is so strong are the author’s interpretation.
The destiny matrix is an esoteric model for self-observation with no scientific evidence base. It is not a forecast, not a diagnosis and not advice on health, money or relationships.

sections.h2: This tail in compatibility
paragraphs: In compatibility, 18-9-9 connects the wish to understand without many words with the task of sharing one’s inner world. The Moon at M brings hints and subtle expectations; the Hermit at N develops the central task through how difficult subjects are considered and answers sought; the Hermit at D concerns trust, shared interests and respect for each person’s individuality. This is our synthesis using Lisovskaya’s pair roles. The two nines answer different questions rather than making a couple “twice as lonely.”

After a difficult day, both people may want quiet. One reads in another room; the other tries not to interrupt but begins wondering whether their company is welcome at all. If each looks for explanations only within themselves, a considerate distance can become filled with guesses. The middle Hermit can help someone think before speaking; as the couple’s task, the Hermit also reminds them that another person’s inner world cannot be discovered by always leaving them alone.

Distinguish between two requests in advance: “I need an hour of quiet” and “I would like you to sit with me.” Then choose a small shared activity that needs no continuous conversation: walking, cooking, or reading nearby and exchanging impressions. The difficulty is waiting for exceptional trust before revealing anything, leaving trust no way to develop. An invitation into a personal interest and an attentive response may serve this combination better than a lengthy examination of feelings.

faq.q: What happened in the past life of a person with the 18-9-9 tail?
faq.a: Popular interpretations speak of secret knowledge that the person used badly: magic used to harm, power over other people’s minds through fear, or a seclusion into which the knowledge was taken and lost. This is the tradition’s legend: neither numbers nor cards establish the events of past lives. It is more useful to read it as a description of what can already be seen now: a habit of knowing more than you say, and of hiding what you have understood where nobody can check it.

faq.q: Does 18-9-9 always mean loneliness?
faq.a: No. The tail describes a habitual way of reacting to uncertainty — withdrawing into silence with your own version. That is roughly one person in eleven, and among them there are any number of family people, sociable people and team players. For them solitude is the comfort zone, not a sentence, and it becomes a resource when it has a time limit and a result. Needing silence is not a flaw; the only flaw is silence with no return.

faq.q: Should I take up magic or esotericism, since the tail is “magical”?
faq.a: No, the tail does not oblige you to practise anything. The “magic” of this combination lies in the ability to see hidden connections, and it works equally well in research, psychology, literature and relationships with the people close to you. If you are drawn to esotericism, the test is the same as for the whole tail: does the practice bring you closer to people and facts, or replace them?

faq.q: Is 18-9-9 different for women and men?
faq.a: No. Gender plays no part in the calculation, and the meaning of the tail does not depend on it. The secret workshop, the test of silence and the disappearing friend are found in everyone alike.

faq.q: Is the 18-9-9 tail linked to anxiety or health?
faq.a: The tail does not diagnose or predict health. Waite’s Moon is fear of the unknown and imagination, not illness, and a calculated number cannot say anything about a particular person’s mental state. If anxiety or isolation is getting in the way of living, sleeping and working, that is a question for a specialist, not for the matrix.

faq.q: Can the 18-9-9 tail be “closed”?
faq.a: The numbers in the matrix do not change; what changes is how the script plays out. Signs of a tail lived through: you ask before you have had time to feel hurt; your pauses are marked with words and a time limit; knowledge leaves the drawer unfinished; you come back from silence with a thought, not a new version; people around you feel lighter, not more anxious.

faq.q: Is the 18-9-9 tail the same as the “18-9-9 program”?
faq.a: A karmic tail is only the triad on the bottom ray of the chart, between the centre and the bottom corner. If the same numbers stand on the relationship line or the money line (for people with 18-9-9 this happens when the year arcanum is 9 or 18, for example in 1980 or 1989), it is the program of that area of life, and it should be read according to the meaning of that line. Still, in such a chart one and the same theme sounds from several sides at once.

the version goes off into silence and grows stronger there unchecked

report: The 18-9-9 tail comes with a legend: a mage who took his knowledge to the grave. In a past life, it says, the soul held secret knowledge and misused it: in some versions through black magic and power over other minds through fear, in others by withdrawing from people and passing the knowledge to nobody. Hence the name “Forbidden Knowledge”. The legend cannot be checked: a birth date says nothing about the past. But the name has a footing in the cards themselves.

Benebell Wen calls the Moon the signifier of “society’s magi, priest, or shaman”. For her the High Priestess holds esoteric knowledge, while the Moon is “the beginning manifestation into consciousness of that esoteric knowledge”. In 1910 Waite retold readings in which the Hermit’s lantern holds “the Light of Occult Science” and his staff is “a Magic Wand”.

Then comes the turn. The commonest reading of the Hermit — “occult isolation”, the protection of “personal magnetism” against admixture — Waite dismisses as a frivolous rendering inherited from Éliphas Lévi. Today the same idea goes by “protect your energy”. For 18-9-9 no explanation is more tempting: it justifies the tail’s mechanism. Waite objects that the true mysteries “secure their own protection from those who are unprepared”. Hiding them is pointless.

Hence our reading. In 18-9-9 nobody forbade the knowledge from outside. **The person sets the ban themselves — not on knowing, but on showing, checking and giving away.** This tail is home to someone who knows more than they say.

report.h3: A guess that feels like knowing

report: The tail’s entry is the Moon. Waite describes a road between two towers, running into the unknown. The dog and the wolf by the road are, for him, “the fears of the natural mind”, “when there is only reflected light to guide it”.

A reply came back shorter than usual. The boss said hello more drily than yesterday. Someone with 18-9-9 notices such things first, and often correctly — that is the Moon’s real strength. But reflected light shows that something is there, not what it is. An old fear fills the gap. In our reading the dog and the wolf are two voices: “you’re not wanted here” and “you’re being used here”. In seconds a version takes shape, and it feels like knowledge, not a guess.

report.h3: Silence feeds the version details, not facts

report: Then the person does not ask but withdraws to work it out alone. Wen reads the Hermit’s lantern two ways: a light shining for others in the dark — or someone who “sees the world through his or her own light”. The middle nine of the tail is the second lantern, the one under the cloak. The longer the person thinks alone, the neater the first-seconds story looks and the more dangerous a simple question seems.

Waite writes of a creature crawling from the water: a vague movement from the depths that “strives to attain manifestation”, “but as a rule it sinks back whence it came”. So the sentence “I felt uneasy — has something happened?” almost reaches the shore, then slips back under. Wen gives this crayfish a tough outer shell, and beneath it “a profound vulnerability that the Seeker is trying to conceal from others”.

Those around them do not know they have already been tried and convicted in absentia. They meet a polite distance and answer in kind, and the returned coolness becomes proof: “I knew it.” **The silence produces exactly the estrangement the person feared.**

report.h3: Withdrawal here feels like coming home, not running away

report: Everyone with 18-9-9 has the Hermit in the centre of the chart as well. The centre is the comfort zone, so withdrawing feels not like a problem but like rest. The tail runs not on suffering but on comfort, which is why it goes unnoticed for so long. The tail’s Moon is made of two Hermits, the centre and the root: 9 + 9 = 18.
