Fog is born where solitude meets solitude. A play of numbers, not a proof — but an exact one.

The same Moon opens the relationship line: here the entry into the script and the entry into closeness coincide. The most recognisable scene is **the test of silence**. Something has hurt, but instead of speaking the person goes quiet and watches whether the partner will notice. The partner has no idea an exam is under way — and fails a test nobody mentioned. With each round the Moon grows more convincing: the silence has never once let it be wrong out loud.

report.h3: Solitude with a return address

report: At the root stands the Hermit again, but with a different lantern. For Waite this is a card of **attainment rather than of quest**: the Hermit does not wander in the dark but stands on a height and holds up a lantern with a star in it. Waite sums up this beacon in one phrase: “where I am, you also may be.” Unlike earlier familiar images, where the cloak partly wraps the lantern, Waite’s is uncovered. From the outside the two Hermits look the same: both are silent. The middle one withdraws from people. The root one withdraws to come back to them.

The task of 18-9-9 is not to stop being a Hermit but to come back from the silence with a result. When a partner who usually writes at length replies “ok”, one sentence is enough: “Short on words today. Tired, or has something happened?” The Moon’s observation was right; only the explanation, invented alone, was wrong.

An analyst spots an error in the accounts first and quietly rechecks; three weeks later everyone sees it: “I saw it.” The lived-through version sounds modest: “Take a look at line fourteen, I don’t think it adds up.”
The author’s own practices, not a ritual:

ul: when stepping away to think, name a time: “I’ll come back to this tomorrow evening”; solitude with a deadline is the Hermit, without one, the cloak;
within a day, ask one neutral question: “I noticed that… Does it mean something, or did I imagine it?”;
show unfinished work — a draft, a sketch, a half-formed idea: the root nine does not require finishing first.

report: If anxiety or isolation gets in the way of living, sleeping and working, that is a question for a specialist, not for the matrix.

report.h3: People who notice before it gets light

report: In the lived-through version the Moon sees what is hidden: subtext, a faint signal, the error on line fourteen. The middle Hermit can work alone for a long time; the root one turns this into light for others. Wen writes that the first clarity comes from the moon, from the reflection, rather than from the sun itself. People with 18-9-9 are often that first clarity.

For everyone with this tail, all four purposes can only be the Hermit or the Moon. In our reading **the tail here is not someone else’s load but a raw version of one’s own gift**: the same fog and the same cloak, in mature form, become the ability to see the hidden and give light to others.

This is the person people call when it is dark. They are not frightened by someone else’s anxiety, because they know it from the inside. Someone who once stood by a night road with only reflected light, while the dog and the wolf howled, becomes the one who holds a lantern on that road for others.

items.title: Karmic tail 21-10-16 in the destiny matrix: the “Spiritual Priest” who builds the eternal on a wheel

seo.title: 21-10-16 in the Destiny Matrix: the “Spiritual Priest” Karmic Tail
seo.description: Karmic tail 21-10-16: why a big “forever” collapses at a turn of the wheel and how to hold the whole without making it a monument. Calculation, script, practice.

items.short: The karmic tail 21-10-16 is the script of a person who builds a whole “forever” on a turning foundation. At the entry stands the World (21): you quickly put together a finished picture — a business, a union, a system of views where everything fits. In the middle is the Wheel of Fortune (10): circumstances turn, and the picture starts to lag behind life. At the root is the Tower (16): if you defend the form to the last, the whole structure falls at once. The task of the tail is to keep the scale but hold the whole loosely and rebuild it at every turn, while this is still a repair and not a collapse.

sections.h2: How to tell that you have 21-10-16
paragraphs: The check takes half a minute. Take three numbers from your birth date: the day (if it is over 22, add its digits), the number of the month and the sum of the digits of the year (if it is over 22, add the digits again). **If the three numbers add up to exactly 16, your karmic tail is 21-10-16.** No other tail comes from this sum, and the other way round: 21-10-16 comes only from it.

Example: 05.04.1987. Day — 5, month — 4, year: 1 + 9 + 8 + 7 = 25, reduced to 2 + 5 = 7. In total 5 + 4 + 7 = 16. Then by the method’s formula: the karmic task D = 16, the centre E = 16 + 16 = 32 → 5, the lower inner point M = 16 + 5 = 21, the middle of the tail N = 16 + 21 = 37 → 10. The tail is read from the centre downwards, M–N–D: 21-10-16. The same result comes from, for example, 25.03.2004: the day 25 reduces to 7, and 7 + 3 + 6 = 16.

ul: Among all dates from 1950 to 2025 — 2.3%, roughly one in 44. By frequency this is 19th place out of the 26 tails the formula produces at all.

Among people born since 2000 it is two and a half times as common: 3.7% against 1.5% among those born in 1950–1999. The reason is arithmetic: the digits of the years of the 2000s add up to a small number, and it is easy to make up sixteen with the day and month.

In some years this tail does not occur at all: 1950–1957, 1960–1966, 1970–1975, 1980–1984 and 1990–1993. The digit sum of these years after reducing is 15 or more, which leaves no room for the day and month.
Nor does it occur for people born from the 14th to the 22nd of any month, and in December it came up only three times in 76 years.

paragraphs: If a calculator showed you 21-10-16 but your date does not pass this check, it calculates by a different scheme. Everything below applies to Ladini’s classic scheme, where the tail is the points M, N and D on the bottom ray of the chart.

paragraphs.h3: What comes into the chart together with the tail

paragraphs: Sixteen at point D rigidly sets a few more numbers. They are the same for everyone with 21-10-16, and without them the tail reads incompletely:

head: Where in the chart
Number
What it gives the reading
rows: Leaning on a teaching, rules, a proven order. More on this in the section on the tail’s popular name.
This is the same point M where the tail begins: in close relationships the script switches on first.
The Tower also stands in the line from which the personal purpose is built.
The centre of the chart twice, and the Wheel in the emotions column.

paragraphs: A number repeating in different places does not mean the quality doubles: in each position the arcanum has its own role. But if fives, sixteens and twenty-ones catch your eye in your chart, the reason is the arithmetic of the tail, not a random coincidence.

sections.h2: Three roles: what each arcanum does here specifically

head: Position
Arcanum
Role in the 21-10-16 tail
rows: The first move: assemble a whole. See how everything fits and give it a finished form. The failure begins when the finished is mistaken for the unchanging.
Keeps the repetition going. Circumstances turn, the turn is put down to bad luck or a “bad patch”, and the old form is built again.
The root task: recognise a false foundation and take it apart yourself, while this is a review and not a wreck.

paragraphs: Taken separately, there is nothing alarming in these arcana. The World is fullness and completion, the Wheel is the movement of life, the Tower is honesty about what has been built wrongly. The tension comes from the order they stand in.

On the Waite–Smith deck the World and the Wheel share a detail: in the four corners of both cards are the same creatures from Ezekiel’s vision — an angel, an eagle, a lion and a bull. On the Wheel they hold open books; on the World there are no books any more. In the order of the major arcana the Wheel comes tenth and the World last: first study, then the wreath. In the 21-10-16 tail the order is reversed. The person starts with the feeling that the picture is complete and clear, and life sends them back to the books again and again. This is our reading of the picture; the deck has no such rule, but it captures the character of the combination exactly: **from graduation back to the school desk**.

sections.h2: The main image: a sphinx on a pedestal
paragraphs: Waite has a remark that explains this tail better than any list of qualities. On his Wheel of Fortune the sphinx sits right on the wheel — it is the equilibrium within the movement. Waite notes that the sphinx is sometimes drawn lying on a fixed pedestal above the wheel, and that this spoils the symbol, because it kills the main idea of the card — **stability amidst movement**.

The 21-10-16 tail means building the sphinx a pedestal again and again. The World gives a taste for the whole, the Wheel does not stop, and the person looks for a footing above the rotation: a decision that will never need revisiting, a union “for life” in an unchanging form, a business of one format, the one true picture of the world. The pedestal seems like protection against change. In fact it is the weakest point of the structure; it just stays hidden until the wheel turns far enough.

The Tower strikes precisely at pedestals. In Pamela Colman Smith’s drawing the lightning knocks the crown off the top of the tower — the thing that crowns the building and declares it finished. The lightning goes to whatever has been declared final.

The World itself gives a hint for the way out. The figure in its wreath is not standing but dancing. Waite cites Éliphas Lévi’s idea: a garland of roses is a chain that is harder to break than a chain of iron. **Wholeness that moves is stronger than wholeness that has been put in chains.** That is the whole task of the tail: to hold the whole the way a dancer holds balance — without freezing.

sections.h2: How the circle winds up

ol: **Assembly.** Something big comes together: a business, a relationship, a career, a view of life. Everything fits, and the World gives a rare feeling: this is it, now it is clear how things should be.

**Coronation.** The form is declared final. Rules appear, promises of “forever”, a self-image: “I’m that kind of person”, “that’s how we do things”, “this is my life’s work”. The sphinx climbs onto the pedestal.

**The turn.** The Wheel does its job: people change, the market changes, age, your own desires. The first signals are noticed but get a convenient explanation: “a temporary bad patch”, “bad luck”, “we just need to ride it out”.

**Building on top.** Instead of reviewing the foundation, the form is reinforced: more effort, more rules, more investment, louder confidence. The more visible the shift below, the higher the floor added above.

**The strike.** The gap between the form and life grows bigger than the structure can bear, and it falls all at once. From the outside — suddenly. From the inside — after a long, quiet “I saw this coming”.

paragraphs: After that the circle either starts again, with a new and equally final form on the next turn, or goes into one of the false exits described below.

The key link is the third step. Waite writes that behind the symbol of the Wheel lies the denial of chance and of fatalism. And “just bad luck” and “that’s fate” are exactly the explanation the repetition rests on: if the collapse was random, there is nothing to review, and the next form can be built the same way. **The circle breaks between the third and fourth steps** — when the shift is already visible but the new floor has not yet been built. One question is useful for going over your own stories: how much time passed between “I noticed” and “I admitted it”? In this tail, that is exactly where all the damage builds up.

sections.h2: Three false exits: freeze, run, stop believing
paragraphs: After one or two collapses you want to find a way never to go round the circle again. The trouble is that all three usual ways are varieties of the same pedestal.

**Freeze.** Build nothing on a large scale any more, cling to what survived and go nowhere. In Waite’s divinatory list the reversed World carries exactly these words: inertia, fixity, stagnation, permanence. This is the World without the dance: the whole is preserved at the cost of the life inside it.

**Run.** Change the scenery: the city, the job, the partner, the country. The upright World in the same list carries voyage, emigration, flight, change of place, so this exit is very familiar to the tail. A move can in itself be the best decision. The trap is elsewhere: if the old scheme moves to the new place with you, the Wheel will turn there too.

**Stop believing.** Decide that nothing lasting exists and never again invest in anything fully: “it will collapse anyway”. Among the meanings of the reversed World, Benebell Wen names fear of change and philosophical scepticism. Cynicism looks like sobriety but works like dogma: it is a ready-made answer that spares you from looking at what is happening now. The same pedestal, only empty.
All three have the same real exit: rebuild the whole to fit the turn.

sections.h2: Why it is called the “Spiritual Priest”
paragraphs: Popular readings call the 21-10-16 tail the “Spiritual Priest”, less often the “Spiritual Teacher”, and usually do not explain where the name comes from. It has support in the chart itself: everyone with this tail has arcanum 5 in the centre. Waite lists the old names of the fifth card — the High Priest, the Hierophant, the Spiritual Father. The name of the tail is assembled from them almost word for word. Whether this is a coincidence or the source of the name cannot be said, but it matters for reading the tail.

In Waite the Hierophant is the open, recognised form of a teaching: tradition, hierarchy, passing on knowledge through an institution. Waite calls him the sum of theology when it has passed into the utmost rigidity of expression, and points to a possible error: the bearer of the office may forget that he only represents something greater and act as if he contained the whole meaning of his symbol. Waite describes the Tower in the same terms — as the rending of a House of Doctrine, or more precisely a House of Falsehood. The two people falling from it he reads as the letter that has lost its force and its false interpretation.

Now the whole combination reads as one sentence. The comfort zone is teaching and order (5). The habitual entry is to assemble a finished system out of experience (21). Life turns (10). And if the system has already become a house where nothing can be rebuilt, it turns into a House of Falsehood and falls (16). The teaching here is not necessarily religion or esoterica. It is any scheme of “how it’s done right”: how to raise children, run a business, build a marriage, handle money, live in general.
You can recognise this side of the tail by small things:

ul: you explain more often than you ask, and get irritated when people live “wrongly”;
a rule that once saved you gets applied where circumstances have long been different;
admitting “I was wrong” is harder than starting everything from scratch;
you change teachers and systems, and each next one seems final.

paragraphs: In this light the root task sounds like this: **be a priest who inspects his own temple**. Do not give up your knowledge and do not be shy about passing it on, but review your own teaching before the lightning does it for you.

paragraphs.h3: And what about a past life?

paragraphs: The tradition links the tail to a past incarnation, and about 21-10-16 it usually tells one of two stories: the person possessed knowledge and did not pass it on — or passed it on in a way that turned knowledge into power over others. Neither can be checked, and neither follows from the calculation. But both are about the same thing as the whole tail: a person’s relationship with their own teaching. Hiding knowledge and imposing it are two sides of one mistake: knowledge stops being checked against living people. To work with the tail you do not need to believe in reincarnation: this plot is visible within a single life.

sections.h2: Where the script shows up
paragraphs: Below are typical forms of the circle. These are examples: it only makes sense to recognise yourself in them where the mechanism matches — a final form, a turn, building on top, a strike.

The business is conceived broadly and for the long term, but for a specific moment: that market, that team, that partner. The moment passes, but the model stays the same; it is defended, expanded, more money is put in. The closure then looks sudden, although the foundation shifted a year or two before. Another version is a career built around one role “for life”: when the role becomes outdated, the person’s idea of themselves collapses along with it.

This is where the script switches on first: point M, where the tail begins, also opens the relationship line. A union quickly becomes a finished picture — “this is how it will be for us”: roles, habits, plans, a shared history. But both people change, and a picture that allows no edits starts to argue with living people. The crisis seems like a bolt from the blue, although the lightning struck a pedestal the couple built themselves. The false exit here is a new partner with the same picture. The living version is a couple who, from time to time, honestly rebuild their agreements: what has changed for us, and what from before no longer works.

A bet on one scheme that once worked: one profession, one big client, one way of earning, declared the only reliable one. As long as the Wheel turns the right way, the scheme seems eternal. The script has nothing to do with poverty or wealth: it is about a support that nobody checks while it holds.

paragraphs.h3: In beliefs and the search for yourself

paragraphs: The subtlest form is changing teachings. Psychology, religion, business philosophy, esoterica, a particular mentor: each new teaching is accepted as the final truth, disappointment in it is lived as a collapse, after which the search for the next one begins. It also happens the other way round: the person assembles a system themselves and begins teaching it to others, without noticing that it describes their own past experience better than other people’s present.

Changing places as a way to solve everything at once. Sometimes it really does set you free. The script gives itself away if, a couple of years later, the same structure with the same crack stands in the new place.

sections.h2: The strength: what 21-10-16 looks like when worked through
paragraphs: In its mature form the same set of arcana gives a rare combination — scale without petrification. Such people can:

ul: **build big things with seams** — a business, a family, a team that can be rebuilt without demolition, because room for change was built in from the start;
**notice the turn before others** — a mature Wheel senses that conditions have changed and does not waste a year on denial;
**close cycles** — the World at its best is about completion: finish, sum up, let go and start the next thing without baggage;
**keep a cool head in a crisis** — someone who has lived through several collapses knows that it is the form that falls, not everything;
**talk about the crack out loud** — the Tower’s honesty makes them valuable where everyone else pretends that all is well;
**teach and relearn** — a Priest who checks his own teaching passes knowledge on without dogma and can say “I used to think differently”.

paragraphs: This combination comes in handy wherever living systems are rebuilt on the move: in reorganisations, education, crisis management, editing, long-horizon projects. No list of “right” professions follows from it.

sections.h2: A support or a pedestal: how to tell them apart
paragraphs: The World is not the enemy in this tail: without the pull towards the whole there would be neither a big business nor a long relationship. The only question is what the structure stands on. A few signs:

head: A living whole
A pedestal
rows: Has a condition, named in advance, under which it is reviewed
“Forever”, “it has always been so and always will be”
Change is discussed as part of life
Change is seen as betrayal or a threat
Rests on how much has already been invested
Mistakes are admitted as you go, one at a time
Mistakes pile up until there are too many
Can only be kept whole or lost whole
Rules explain why they are needed
Rules appeal to “that’s the right way”

paragraphs: If more of the matches are in the right-hand column, it is time to review the structure while it can still be done piece by piece.

sections.h2: How to work with the 21-10-16 tail
paragraphs: Each practice below targets a specific link of the circle. None of them requires heroics: the point is frequent small reviews instead of one big one after a collapse.

ol: **A foundation passport.** For each big structure — a job, an agreement in a couple, a major plan, a belief — write down: “This rests on … I will review it if …”. A condition for review, named in advance, turns a turn of the Wheel from a catastrophe into an expected event.

**Reviews on the calendar of turns.** Tie a review to natural turning points: your birthday, the end of the year, the end of a project, the birth of a child, a change of job. Three questions: what has changed around me, what has changed in me, which of my rules was written for the previous turn?

**The letter and the interpretation.** Take a belief you defend especially fiercely and split it into two parts: what actually happened once, and what conclusion you drew from it. Both figures fall from the Tower — the letter and the interpretation. Often only the second is out of date, and it can be replaced without a collapse.

**A small tower.** Once a season, deliberately dismantle one thing that is held up only by inertia: a duty, a role, a habit, a rule in the family or the team, a direction in your business. A small voluntary demolition is a vaccination against a big one.

**Closing the circle.** When something ends, end it explicitly: a summing-up, gratitude, what I take forward, what I leave behind. What is complete does not need defending; it has already happened. This is how the World works in its sound version.

**An inventory before running.** Before changing city, job or partner, list three things you will do in the new place the same way as in the old one. If the list includes what made the old one collapse, it is the list that needs changing first.
**Teach on request.** Before explaining to someone how it should be done, ask whether they want advice. And test your knowledge on new cases: on old examples it always works.

**A support in motion.** Write down what stayed with you through every turn: skills, values, people, a way of thinking. This is your sphinx — stability that rides along with the wheel. You can lean on it without building a pedestal.

ul: Which two or three stories in my life ended in a “sudden” collapse, and when did I first notice the crack?
What that I am defending now rests on what has been invested rather than on what is alive?
Which of my rules was right for a past stage and still applies without being checked?
Where do I explain what is happening as bad luck so as not to change anything?
What could I take apart myself now, while it is still small?

paragraphs: A sign that the work is going well: reviews happen earlier and on a smaller scale, and the phrase “it all collapsed in one day” gives way to “we changed that”.

sections.h2: How 21-10-16 differs from similar tails

head: Tail
What they share
The difference
rows: The same entry (the World) and the same middle (the Wheel)
The Chariot at the root: the task is to choose a direction among the turns. In 21-10-16 the direction is usually chosen; what needs reviewing is the foundation it stands on.
The World at the entry, the Wheel in the tail
The repetition is held by the Emperor — control and a rigid frame, and the Wheel stands at the root: the task is to learn to move with the turn rather than hold on to the layout.
The repetition is held by the speed of the Chariot, with Death at the root: the task is to bring the circle to a mature ending without resetting it halfway.

There the Tower is in the middle, as the mechanism: the expectation of a break, which makes a person put off change until the last moment. In 21-10-16 the Tower is the root task, and the repetition is held by the Wheel.

paragraphs: But 16-10-21 never occurs as a karmic tail in this scheme: the first number of a tail is always a multiple of three — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 21 — and 16 is not among them. The triple 16-10-21 occurs in other places in the chart or in other calculation systems; the roles of the numbers there are different, and this reading of 21-10-16 does not carry over to it.

sections.h2: Myths about the 21-10-16 tail

ul: **“This is a tail of disasters; everything in life will keep collapsing.”** The Tower stands at the root as a task, not a forecast. The tail describes a tendency to hold on to a form longer than it holds, and the earlier a person reviews it themselves, the less is left to the sudden.

**“The Tower is always for the best.”** The opposite extreme. In Waite the Tower is a card of calamity and unforeseen catastrophe; he does not call it a “useful shake-up”. The point of working through the tail is not to let things come to a crash, not to learn to admire crashes.
**“In a past life you were a tyrant or an apostate priest.”** Such stories do not follow from the calculation and give nothing to work with. What is visible in this life is enough.

**“You need to go into spirituality, become a psychologist or a priest.”** The “Priest” in the tail’s name speaks of your relationship with your own teaching; profession has nothing to do with it. You can be a dogmatist in accounting and a living person in a monastery.
**“The tail is closed with a 21-day ritual.”** The tail is a habitual script, not a debt paid off in one instalment. It weakens as you learn to recognise it at the early steps and act differently.

**“Sixteen in the tail means you must break everything yourself.”** Breaking things out of boredom or for a shake-up is a distortion of the Tower. A mature Tower dismantles only what has stopped holding, and piece by piece.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: **Calculation** — Natalia Ladini’s classic destiny matrix scheme: D = A + B + C, the centre E = A + B + C + D, the tail M–N–D, where M = D + E and N = D + M; sums over 22 are reduced by adding their digits. Frequencies were calculated by running through all dates from 1950 to 2025 with the same formula.

**Arcana meanings** — Arthur Edward Waite’s book The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910) and Pamela Colman Smith’s drawings for his deck; additional points from Benebell Wen’s book Holistic Tarot (2015).

**The script of the tail** — the author’s interpretation. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the destiny matrix or karmic tails: the meanings of the cards come from their books, and linking the three positions into one script is our work.
**The popular name** “Spiritual Priest” comes from popular readings; its origin is not documented anywhere.

paragraphs: The destiny matrix is an esoteric system of interpretation, not a scientific method. The tail describes a tendency and gives you a language to notice it; it does not assign events.

sections.h2: This tail in compatibility
paragraphs: For a couple, 21-10-16 raises the question of what keeps a shared foundation steady when plans change. The World at M concerns an expansive horizon of wishes; the Wheel of Fortune at N develops the task through changing circumstances and recurring highs and lows; the Tower at D invites a revision of fragile assumptions and support built on real participation. This connection is our interpretation using Lisovskaya’s pair positions, rather than a ready-made meaning for the triple from her book.

Suppose the partners are preparing a long trip, but their usual schedule no longer works. They can revise dates and costs, or hear every adjustment as rejection of the shared dream. The World’s broad horizon then narrows to one scenario, the Wheel’s changes become irritating in themselves, and the image of the relationship is challenged: “If we are a team, everything should go to plan.” The Tower helps reveal how fragile that condition is; it predicts neither separation nor disaster.

Separate the purpose of the plan from the single method imagined for achieving it. Then prepare an alternative with clear dates and contributions from both people. The difficulty is discussing adjustments only when exhausted, when every suggestion can sound like criticism. A brief regular check-in can give the couple something firmer to rely on: what has changed, where help is needed, and what still matters to both. The larger goal then depends less on events unfolding without a hitch.

faq.q: How do I know whether my karmic tail is 21-10-16?
faq.a: Add up the arcanum of your birth day (a day over 22 is reduced by adding its digits), the number of the month and the reduced sum of the digits of the year. If you get exactly 16, your tail is 21-10-16. In a ready-made chart the sign is the same: 16 at the lower outer point D and 5 in the centre.

faq.q: Are 21-10-16 and 16-10-21 the same tail?
faq.a: No. In the M–N–D scheme the first number of the tail is always a multiple of three, so 16-10-21 never occurs as a karmic tail here. This triple occurs in other places in the chart or in other calculation systems; the roles of the numbers there are different, and this reading of 21-10-16 does not carry over to it.

faq.q: Will there necessarily be upheavals in my life?
faq.a: No. The Tower at the root describes a task; the tail makes no forecasts. The tail shows a weak spot: the habit of defending a form longer than it holds. The earlier you review the foundations yourself, the less work is left for the lightning. No reading promises complete protection from change: the Wheel turns for everyone.

faq.q: Why is the tail called the “Spiritual Priest”?
faq.a: Readings usually do not explain the name. It has support in the chart itself: everyone with 21-10-16 has arcanum 5 in the centre, the Hierophant, whom Waite also calls the High Priest and the Spiritual Father. This coincidence fits well with the main plot of the tail — a relationship with your own teaching: to assemble a system out of experience and not turn it into a house that cannot be rebuilt.

faq.q: I found 21-10-16 in a compatibility matrix. Is it the same tail?
faq.a: Not quite. In a personal chart the tail is points M, N and D, calculated from one date. In a compatibility matrix the numbers are calculated from two dates, and the same triple then describes the couple’s script, while each partner keeps their own personal tail. It needs to be read by the rules of that scheme; the reading above applies to the personal chart.

faq.q: Is the tail different for men and women?
faq.a: No. Sex plays no part in the calculation and changes neither the numbers nor the mechanism. The circumstances in which the script shows up can differ, but the combination itself — a final form, a turn, building on top, a strike — is the same for everyone.

faq.q: What should I do if my child has 21-10-16?
faq.a: Children have it more often than adults: among birth dates since 2000, roughly one in 27. There is no cause for alarm in this. The most useful thing is to show the child in practice that rules can change and are reviewed together: explain why things are now different in the family, let them redo what they have started, calmly bring to an end what has finished. Then “everything collapsed” will not become the only way of change they know.

faq.q: Can a karmic tail be closed?
faq.a: Not with a single action: a habitual script weakens gradually. A sign that the work is going well: reviews happen earlier and on a smaller scale, and less and less time passes between “I noticed the crack” and “I admitted it”.

report: The 21-10-16 tail has a popular name, the “Spiritual Priest”, and nobody has recorded where it came from. Tradition ties the tail to a past life: the person supposedly held knowledge and kept it back — or passed it on so that it became power over others. None of this can be checked. But the name has a firmer footing than legend. It stands in the chart itself.

Everyone with this tail has the fifth arcanum in the centre of the chart. Waite lists its old names: the High Priest, the Hierophant, the Spiritual Father. The tail’s name is built from them almost word for word. Coincidence or source of the name — there is no telling, but it matters for reading the tail.

Waite calls the Hierophant the sum of theology “when it has passed into the utmost rigidity of expression”, and points to a possible error: the pontiff may forget that he only represents something greater and act as if he contained the whole meaning of his symbol. He describes the Tower, the root of this tail, in the same terms: the rending of a House of Doctrine, or rather a House of Falsehood. The two people falling from it he reads as “the literal word made void” and “its false interpretation”.

Now the tail reads as one sentence. The comfort zone is teaching and order (5). The habitual entry is building a finished system from experience (21, The World). Life turns (10, The Wheel of Fortune). And if the system is now a house where nothing can be rebuilt, it becomes a House of Falsehood and falls (16, The Tower). The teaching here is not necessarily religion. It is any scheme of “how it’s done right”: raising children, running a business, building a marriage.

report.h3: Building the sphinx a pedestal

report: On Waite’s Wheel of Fortune the sphinx sits on the wheel itself, the equilibrium within the movement. Sometimes, Waite notes, it is drawn lying on a pedestal above, which “defrauds the symbolism by stultifying the essential idea of stability amidst movement”.

The 21-10-16 tail builds the sphinx a pedestal again and again: a decision never to be revisited, a union “for life”, the one true picture of the world. The pedestal looks like protection against change. In fact it is the weakest point of the structure, hidden until the wheel turns far enough.

The Tower strikes precisely at pedestals. In Pamela Colman Smith’s drawing the lightning knocks the crown off the tower — the piece that tops the building and declares it finished. Waite does not call this card a useful shake-up: it is “a card in particular of unforeseen catastrophe”.

In the Waite–Smith deck, Ezekiel’s four creatures fill the corners of both the World and the Wheel. On the Wheel they hold open books; on the World the books are gone. The Wheel comes tenth, the World last: first study, then the wreath. In the tail the order is reversed. This is our reading, not a rule of the deck, but it captures the combination exactly: **from graduation back to the school desk**.

report.h3: The damage builds up between “I noticed” and “I admitted it”

report: The circle winds up in five steps:

ol: Assembly. Something big comes together — a business, a union, a view of life: “this is it, now it is clear how things should be”.
Coronation. The form is declared final: “forever”, “that’s how we do things”, “this is my life’s work”.
The turn. People change, and so do the market, age, desires. The first signals get a convenient explanation: “a temporary bad patch”, “bad luck”.
Building on top. Instead of reviewing the foundation, the form is reinforced. The more visible the shift below, the higher the floor added above.
The strike. The structure falls all at once. From the outside — suddenly. From the inside — after a long, quiet “I saw this coming”.

report: Behind the Wheel, Waite writes, lies the denial of chance and of fatalism. And “just bad luck” is exactly the explanation the repetition rests on: if the collapse was random, there is nothing to review, and the next form can be built the same way. **The circle breaks between the third and fourth steps** — when the shift is already visible but the new floor is not yet built.

The script switches on first in relationships: the point where the tail begins also opens the relationship line. A union quickly becomes a finished picture — “this is how it will be for us” — while the people in it keep changing. The crisis seems like a bolt from the blue, although the lightning struck a pedestal the couple built themselves. A subtler form: someone builds a system and teaches it, not noticing that it describes their own past better than other people’s present.

report.h3: Three escapes, one pedestal

report: After a collapse or two comes the urge to leave the circle for good. There are three ways to try.
Freeze — build nothing on a large scale any more. Waite’s divinatory list gives the reversed World exactly these words: inertia, fixity, stagnation, permanence. This is the World without the dance.

Run — change the city, the job, the partner. The upright World in the same list has voyage, emigration, flight, change of place. A move can be the right decision, but if the old scheme moves too, the Wheel will turn there as well.

Stop believing — decide that nothing lasting exists. For the reversed World, Benebell Wen lists fear of change and philosophical scepticism. Cynicism looks like sobriety but works like dogma: a ready-made answer saves the trouble of looking at what is happening now. The same pedestal, only empty.

report.h3: A chain of roses is stronger than iron

report: The hint comes from the World itself. In the Waite–Smith deck the figure in its wreath is not standing but dancing. Waite cites Éliphas Lévi: a garland of roses is a chain “less easily broken than a chain of iron”. **Wholeness that moves is stronger than wholeness that has been put in chains.**
The way out is frequent small reviews instead of one big one after a collapse:

ul: for every big structure, write down in advance: “This rests on … I will review it if …”. A named condition makes a turn of the Wheel an expected event rather than a catastrophe;

split a fiercely defended belief in two: what actually happened and what was concluded from it. Both fall from the Tower, the letter and the interpretation, but often only the second is out of date and can be replaced without a collapse;
once a season, dismantle one thing held up only by inertia. A small voluntary demolition is a vaccination against a big one;
before a move or a new union, list three things that will be done there exactly as before. If the list includes what made the old one collapse, it is the list that needs changing first.

report: Mature, the same arcana give a rare combination — scale without petrification. Such people build big things with seams, to rebuild without demolition; they notice the turn before others and name the crack out loud. In a crisis they know it is the form that falls, not everything. The root task of the tail is to **be a priest who inspects his own temple**: not to be shy about passing knowledge on, but to review one’s own teaching before the lightning does.

items.title: Karmic tail 21-10-7 in the destiny matrix: “the Warrior of Faith”, a wheel without a chariot and a crown at the end of the road

seo.title: 21-10-7 in the destiny matrix: the “Warrior of Faith” karmic tail
seo.description: Karmic tail 21-10-7: why knowing “how things should be” leads in circles and how to turn faith into your own road. A date check, every birth date, practices.

items.short: 21-10-7 is the karmic tail that popular readings of the destiny matrix call “the Warrior of Faith”. Its script goes like this. Early on, a person receives a picture of the whole: what the world should be like, what a right life looks like, what real love is, what cause is worth living for. That is the entry, the World (21). But life around them turns by its own laws, and the picture runs into a turn again and again. That is the mechanism, the Wheel of Fortune (10). At the turn the tail has two habits: to push the wheel by force — prove, remake, fight for its truth — or to wait for the wheel to carry it where it needs to go. Both bring it back to the same circle. At the root stands the Chariot (7): the task is to turn faith into a road, that is, to choose your own stretch of the way and drive it yourself. This is one of the rarest tails, about one birth date in 275. People born in May, June and July never have it, and from 2022 to 2029 not a single person with it was or will be born. And everyone who has it has Temperance in the centre of the chart — the very measure that the “warrior of faith” lacks.

sections.h2: Do you have the 21-10-7 tail? A ten-second check
paragraphs: No calculator needed. 21-10-7 comes up if and only if the first three numbers of the matrix add up to **7 or 52**.

ol: **Day arcanum** — the day you were born. If it is over 22, add its digits: 30 → 3, 31 → 4.
**Month** — its number, from 1 to 12.
**Year arcanum** — the sum of the digits of the year. If the result is over 22, add the digits again: 1985 → 23 → 5, 1993 → 22, 2001 → 3.

paragraphs: Add the three numbers and check the result:

ul: 21.12.1980: 21 + 12 + 18 = 51 → not this one (this date has the tail 18-6-6).
01.01.1986: 1 + 1 + 6 = 8 → not this one (this date has the tail 6-14-8).

paragraphs: Why it works. The bottom corner of the chart, D, is the reduced sum of the three numbers. The sums 7, 25, 34, 43 and 52 all reduce to seven. After that the centre E decides everything — the same sum plus D. For 7 and 52 it comes out at 14 (7 + 7 = 14; 52 + 7 = 59 → 14), for 25, 34 and 43 at 5. A centre of 14 gives the tail 21-10-7: the entry M = 7 + 14 = 21, the middle N = 7 + 21 = 28 → 10. A centre of 5 gives a different tail with the same Chariot at the root, 12-19-7. There is no other way to 21-10-7: this was checked by going through every day from 1900 to 2100.
The sum doesn’t match, but 21-10-7 is in your chart? Almost certainly you are not looking at the tail — that is the next section, and it concerns most people who search for these numbers.

paragraphs.h3: Every birth date with this tail

paragraphs: The tail is so rare that all its dates fit into two tables. Before 2000 it comes in through the sum 52: the day is the 18th to the 22nd, the month August to December, the sum of the year’s digits 18 to 22.
For 1900–1949 the rule is the same: years whose digits add up to 18 to 22 (for example, 1939 or 1948), and 1 January 1949.
Since 2000 the tail comes in only through the sum 7, that is, through the smallest day, month and year:

ul: **This is one of the rarest tails.** Of all dates from 1950 to 2025 it got 101 out of 27,759, roughly one in 275. That is 24th place out of the 26 tails the formula produces: only 9-18-9 and 6-14-8 are rarer.

**It has two doors at opposite ends of the year.** Before 2000 — from 22 August to 22 December, and only on the 18th–22nd. Since 2000 — from 1 January to 1 April, and only the first days of a month or 30–31 January, which reduce to 3 and 4.
**There are months and days when it never occurs.** People born in May, June and July never get 21-10-7, in any year. Nor do those born on the 5th to the 17th or the 23rd to the 29th.
**A New Year’s tail.** On 1 January it comes up once every nine years: in 1949, 1958, 1967, 1976, 1985, 1994, 2003, 2012, 2021 and 2030. The digits of these years reduce to 5, and 1 + 1 + 5 = 7.

**It has almost disappeared.** Among people born in 1950–1999 it is one date in 231; since 2000, one in 432. After 1 January 2021 the next such date is 1 January 2030, and after that only 22 December 2079. A whole generation of children will grow up without a single “warrior of faith”.

**Temperance in the centre means this tail.** If the centre of the chart holds 14, the tail can only be 21-10-7, and vice versa. There are no dates with a centre of 14 and a different tail; this too was checked on every day from 1900 to 2100.

**7-10-21 is the same tail read from the outside.** There is no tail that starts with 7: the first number of a tail is always a multiple of three. The triple 7-10-21 does not occur at all in the other lines of a personal chart. If you see 7, 10 and 21 on the bottom ray, you are reading your tail from the corner to the centre.

sections.h2: Most often 21-10-7 is not in the tail
paragraphs: This is worth checking before you read on. The same three numbers in the same order appear in one more place of the chart — in the relationship line M–R1–R, also called the love programme. There they occur four times as often as in the tail: 414 dates against 101 over 1950–2025. Of everyone who finds 21-10-7 in their chart, only about one in five has it as the tail.

Telling them apart is easy: look at the centre of the chart. If it is 14, this is your tail, and the reading below is about you. If it is another number, 21-10-7 is in your relationship line. Nobody has this triple in both places at once. People with the 21-10-7 tail always have a different relationship line. And those with 21-10-7 in the relationship line always have one of three neighbouring tails: 21-4-10 (six in ten of them), 21-7-13 or 21-10-16. For example, 07.01.1982 has the tail 21-4-10, 07.01.1976 has 21-7-13, 07.01.1979 has 21-10-16, and all three dates share the same relationship line: 21-10-7.

The relationship line is read by its own rules. Its entry M is shared with the tail, so here too the World means the first move — entering closeness with a picture of a whole shared life. The middle, R1, the point “under the heart”, shows what the couple revolves around once the first attraction has passed: with the Wheel, that is changes, new stages, shared turns. The end point R is where money and relationships cross, what the union comes up against: with the Chariot, that is the question of who steers and where the two of them are going. The result is the script of a couple on the road. It is not a karmic tail and not a debt from the past: the same arcana in another position answer another question. The plot about choosing a direction, which the reading below is devoted to, can be recognised there too, but it has to be read as the story of a couple, not as a personal tail.

sections.h2: Why 21-10-7 is called “the Warrior of Faith”
paragraphs: Popular interpretations explain the name with a past-life legend. The soul supposedly was a preacher, a warrior for the faith or a “moral despot”: it believed devoutly in its own truth and imposed it by force, not by word. Hence the lesson attributed to the tail — tolerance of other people’s views. The legend has a second half, written about less often but recognised just as well: a person “without an inner engine” who changes jobs and places and still can’t find their path. The legend cannot be checked: a birth date says nothing about events of the past. But both its halves, as we will see, are one story.

The name has a footing in the cards themselves. In Waite’s divinatory list the Chariot has “war, triumph, presumption, vengeance”. The World is not a private goal but a picture of the whole world at once, where everything is in its place — that is, faith in the broadest sense. And the third part of the name lies not in the tail but in the centre.

There is a puzzle here. The 12-19-7 tail, called simply “the Warrior”, has the Hierophant, a priest, in the centre of the chart. The “Warrior of Faith” has Temperance there — a winged angel with two cups, the card of measure. So where is the faith? In the same list of Waite’s. To Temperance reversed he gives “Things connected with churches, religions, sects, the priesthood”, and then “disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests”. A calculated number has no reversed position, but the list shows which themes Waite connected with this card at all. Its light is the harmony of different things. Its shadow is the sect: my truth against yours, and interests that do not fit together.

What comes out is almost a formula for the name: a warrior (the Chariot) goes on a campaign for a picture of the whole world (the World), and in the centre stands a card that can become either tolerance or sectarianism (Temperance). Whether this is a coincidence or the source of the name cannot be said: the origin of the popular names of the tails is not documented anywhere. But it helps to read the tail.

sections.h2: The main image: a crown at the start of the road and a crown at the end
paragraphs: The three cards of the tail and the card of the centre are linked by one detail, and it explains 21-10-7 more precisely than any list of traits.

The World in Pamela Colman Smith’s drawing is a dancing figure in an oval garland. Waite reports that Éliphas Lévi “calls the garland a crown”. And he makes an unexpected remark about the card: the World is “perhaps more especially a story of the past”, of the day “when all was declared to be good, when the morning stars sang together”. The World’s garland is a memory of the whole, where everything is in its place.

In the 21-10-7 tail this crown stands at the start. A person enters the script with a ready picture of the right world — not as a dream to walk towards, but as knowledge they already have: “I know how it should be.” Hence the particular tone of the “warrior of faith”. He does not invent anything new; he restores what is right: he gives back to a family, a team, a country, a loved one the order he sees. Wen writes about the World in the position of the past — for her it is a spread, not the matrix, but the match is exact: it is “the state that is predetermined or outlined for the Seeker, though whether the Seeker will walk the path of manifesting that full potential is to be determined by present conditions and choices”. The picture is given. The road is not.

The Chariot at the root says something else about the crown. Waite explains that this card “is really the King in his triumph”, but a king of a particular kind: “the victory which creates kingship as its natural consequence and not the vested royalty of the fourth card”, the Emperor. The Chariot’s crown is not received in advance; it is earned by the road.

And Temperance in the centre shows where the crown really is. Behind the angel with the cups, Waite writes, “A direct path goes up to certain heights on the verge of the horizon, and above there is a great light, through which a crown is seen vaguely.”

So the pictures add up to the task of the tail. At the entry, the person holds the garland in their hands and thinks the road has already been travelled. The root and the centre restore the right order: first the path, then the crown, and it can be made out in advance only vaguely. The link between the pictures is our reading, but it rests on Waite’s own words. The practical conclusion is simple: **a picture of the whole is useful as a horizon and harmful as a ready answer.** With a horizon, you drive. With a ready answer, you fight or you wait.

sections.h2: A wheel without a chariot: how the loop works
paragraphs: The numbers of the tail almost make a sentence. The middle is calculated as the sum of the root and the entry: **Wheel = Chariot + World** (7 + 21 = 28 → 10). A will that drives “towards everything at once” drives in a circle: the whole world has no point on the map you can reach. And a wheel that is not set under a chariot only spins. People rise and fall on it — on Waite’s card one figure goes up with the rim and a serpent goes down — but you cannot get anywhere on it.

ol: **Vision.** A picture takes shape: how to live, work, love, raise children, run a home or a country the right way. It is not an opinion but a sense of the whole — everything fits, and the World gives a rare certainty: I know.
**The turn.** Life turns by its own laws: people think differently, circumstances change, luck comes and goes. The picture runs into the first turn of the wheel.

**The fork.** Here the tail makes its habitual move, and it has two options. Push: prove, persuade, remake — with the Chariot’s force, only aimed at other people. Or wait: “it wasn’t meant to be”, “the time isn’t right”, “this is a sign I should go another way” — and hand the steering to the wheel.

**The revolution.** The wheel comes back to the same point. The campaign ends in defeat, a Pyrrhic victory or a break with those you wanted to convert. The waiting does not pay off. The person ends up where they started, only older.
**A new vision.** The next faith, country, teaching, cause, person — or the old picture under a new banner. And again with the feeling that this time everything will come together.

paragraphs: Wen writes of the Wheel that it can foreshadow “that history will repeat itself”: “the past will become the future and there could be a sense of déjà vu”. For this tail déjà vu is the main sign. “It’s all just like last time” sounds at every new revolution, even though the scenery is different each time.

The tail’s trouble is not a shortage of chances but an excess of them. Curiously, in Waite’s divinatory list the Wheel reversed means not failure but “Increase, abundance, superfluity”. 21-10-7 never runs short of turns, and each one looks like a new path. What is missing is one thing — a destination of your own against which a turn can be judged.

**The loop opens at the third step.** At the fork there is a third move besides “push” and “wait” — to steer: decide what this turn changes about the road and what it does not change about the destination, and drive your stretch yourself. In Colman Smith’s drawing the charioteer has no visible reins: this chariot can only be steered by decision; no harness can replace it. The wheel does not go anywhere. It simply goes under the chariot and starts to carry it.

sections.h2: The Crusader and the Wanderer: one and the same tail
paragraphs: The two halves of the legend — “a warrior who imposes his truth” and “a person without an engine who can’t find their path” — look like two different portraits in popular readings. In fact they are two answers to one and the same turn. Wen observes of the Chariot person: “The Seeker likes to appear in control, but has a tendency to run from his or her problems (or attack the problems with such aggression as to subdue it and therefore avoid true, mature confrontation).” These are the two modes of 21-10-7.

head: The Crusader
The Wanderer
The Charioteer — the tail lived through
rows: What they do at a turn
push the wheel: prove, press, fight
hand the wheel the steering: wait for a sign, leave
change the road, but not the destination
“I know what’s right, and I’ll prove it”
“it wasn’t meant to be”, “this isn’t for me”
“here is my stretch, and here is where it ends”
a promise that keeps being put off
a horizon to check the course by
fellow travellers who will decide for them
companions with roads of their own
years of a life that isn’t theirs
giving up part of the world for the sake of their own stretch

paragraphs: Quite often both modes live in one person in turn: years of campaigning for a righteous cause, defeat, exhaustion, a long spell of “I don’t want anything, let life decide” — and a new faith with which it all begins again.

Waite left a precise caveat about the Chariot: “the liberation which he effects may leave himself in the bondage of the logical understanding”. The Crusader frees others from their delusions and does not notice that he himself is captive to his own rightness. The Wanderer is free of all campaigns and does not notice that the wheel is the one in charge of this freedom.

So the way out is not to swap one mode for the other: become more tolerant of everything, or more decisive in everything. The way out is a question the charioteer asks himself at every turn: **where am I going, and whose decision is it — mine, my idea’s or the circumstances’?**

sections.h2: The hidden fourth card: everyone with 21-10-7 has Temperance in the centre
paragraphs: In the method, the centre is the comfort zone, the point a person returns to. Everyone with this tail has 14 there, Temperance, and this is not a coincidence but arithmetic: a centre of 14 occurs only with this tail. The entry of the tail comes straight out of it: **World = Chariot + Temperance** (7 + 14 = 21).

Together with the formula for the middle, this gives two roads from one point. The Chariot plus the whole world gives a circle. The Chariot plus measure gives the whole. The tail literally points to what the will lacks to reach its goal.

Waite’s Temperance is a winged angel “pouring the essences of life from chalice to chalice”, with “one foot upon the earth and one upon waters”. Waite explains the card’s name this way: “when the rule of it obtains in our consciousness, it tempers, combines and harmonises the psychic and material natures”. And he adds a sentence that sounds like a direct answer to the tail’s question: “Under that rule we know in our rational part something of **whence we came and whither we are going**.”

Hence the paradox of 21-10-7. The centre is harmony, measure, “both at once”. The root is the Chariot, a chosen direction. Until the centre works for the root, Temperance becomes a convenient excuse for the Wanderer: everything can be combined, nothing needs to be chosen, any turn can be accepted. And its shadow from Waite’s list feeds the Crusader: the sect, my truth against yours. When the centre does work, it gives both modes exactly what they lack.

ul: **For the Crusader — tolerance.** Not an empty cup in place of your faith, but two full ones: your own and someone else’s, between which you can pour. Wen describes Temperance as “the fusion of two contrasting elements and bringing them into harmony within the mind or the spirit”.

**For the Wanderer — direction.** That very path to the heights, and the knowledge of where you are going. Wen has a very practical reading of the card for work: often “it isn’t that new skills need to be learned, but rather that the Seeker need only reconcile his or her existing skills with the task at hand”. For the Wanderer this is the answer to endless new beginnings: almost everything needed for a road of their own already lies in their past roads.

paragraphs: Two details for those who love coincidences. In The Symbolism of the Tarot, P. D. Ouspensky called the angel of Temperance Time: “One of the cups the angel holds is the past, the other is the future. The rainbow stream between the cups is the present. You see that it flows both ways” (Wen quotes these words). For a tail that tradition links with the past, the image is exact: the past is not a sentence; it can be poured into the future. And one more: on the angel’s breast Waite sees “the square and triangle of the septenary”, and 4 + 3 = 7. The centre of the tail is 14, that is 7 + 7, and the root is 7. This is not a rule of the method, but it is worth noticing.

sections.h2: Where else the same arcana stand in your chart
paragraphs: A seven in the bottom corner and a fourteen in the centre fix several more numbers. They are the same for everyone with 21-10-7:

head: Where in the chart
Number
What it gives the reading
rows: Always and only with this tail. More in the section above.
Temperance in Physics and Energy, the Wheel in Emotions: the middle of the tail repeats in the chakra of will.
This is point M, the entry of the tail.
This is point D, the root of the tail.
Its entry is shared with the tail. After that, most often 21-5-11, 21-6-3 or 21-4-10, and never 21-10-7.

paragraphs: So all three arcana of the tail and the centre stand in the three lower chakras of the chart. The numbers repeat because of the formula, not because the quality gets stronger: in each position the arcanum has its own role. But if sevens, fourteens and twenty-ones stand out in your chart, the reason is the arithmetic of the tail.

sections.h2: How 21-10-7 shows up in life
paragraphs: The scenes below are sketches. Recognise yourself in them where the mechanism matches: a picture of the whole, a turn, “push or wait”, a new circle.

At work the Crusader is a reformer. He joins a team with a ready understanding of how everything should be set up, and that understanding is often right. The trouble is the method: changes are carried out as a campaign, those who disagree are written down as opponents, every meeting becomes a battle for a righteous cause. After a year or two he leaves feeling misunderstood, and at the new company he starts the same campaign. The wheel turns, and the CV grows.

At work the Wanderer is a person of many beginnings. Every new offer, fashionable direction or crisis looks like a sign: this is it, this is mine. Popular readings of this tail contain an accurate complaint: you can change several jobs, and the sense of your own path still never comes. There is a lot of experience, and it is real; it just has not been put together into one road.

With this script, money often comes in waves, following the revolutions of the wheel: a project took off, a project closed. The numbers do not predict this, but if you recognise it, look at the centre. In Waite’s divinatory list Temperance upright is “Economy, moderation, frugality, management”. For 21-10-7, money is provisions for the road, not campaign spoils, and it helps to manage it as the budget of the chosen stretch, not as a stake on the next turn.

The strong move is the same for both modes: keep the destination fixed and change the road freely. For the reformer — choose one change and see it through. For the Wanderer — judge a new offer not by how bright it is but by whether it brings you closer to what you have chosen.

Here the script switches on earliest of all: the tail’s entry M also opens the relationship line, so for everyone with 21-10-7 it begins with the World. Love begins with a picture of a whole shared life — what a real family, real closeness, a proper home should be.

In a couple the Crusader educates. The partner becomes someone to be brought round to the right picture: the right way to holiday, the right way with money, the right attitude to the relatives. Quarrels turn into sermons, making up into capitulation. In a couple the Wanderer waits: first for a person in whom the whole world will come together, then for the partner to change on their own. At the first serious turn — a move, a child, a crisis for one of the two — out comes “it wasn’t meant to be”.

Imagine a couple where one wants to move to another country and the other does not. The Crusader will gather arguments within a month, win the debate and then live next to a person he has carried off. The Wanderer will give in and wait for years for life to turn everything around by itself. The Charioteer will ask: where are the two of us going over the next two years, and what is each of us ready to give for this road? Temperance in the centre suggests the shape of the answer: two cups, two pictures, and what can be poured from one into the other.

The most recognisable form of the tail. Converting your parents, winning friends over, out-arguing commenters, explaining to your brother the right way to raise children, spend money, vote or believe. The faith here is not necessarily religious: any complete answer to the question “how should one live” will do.

Signs of the Crusader: you prove more often than you ask; your circle gradually narrows to the like-minded; it gets lonely among the “uninitiated”. The sign of the Wanderer is a change of teachings. Each new one is taken as final, disappointment in it feels like a cliff edge, and the next one turns up at the nearest turn.

For this tail the road is not a metaphor. All three cards are about movement: in Waite’s divinatory list the World has “voyage, route, emigration, flight, change of place”, the Wheel is a revolution, the Chariot is the vehicle itself. For 21-10-7 a move may well turn out to be the best decision of their life. The script gives itself away in two variants: a move as a campaign (“over there everything is set up right, and here it isn’t”) and a move as an escape from a turn.

Wen says something precise about the Chariot: it is “travel not for the sake of travel, but for the sake of acquisition”. The test is simple: what are you going to bring back from there — a skill, a business, money, people, understanding? If there is no answer, you are not going for something but away from something.

There are few children with this tail: since 2000, 22 birthdays, all listed above. If your child is among them, the most useful thing is to give them not a crown but a road: small finished tasks with a clear finish, the right to lose an argument, and the experience that changing your mind is not betrayal.

A parent with 21-10-7 should watch for something else: whether they are raising a convert. A child who has been taught from early on the one right picture of the world usually does one of two things with it. Either they carry it further like a banner, or one day they walk away from it — and become a Wanderer.

sections.h2: The road or the circle: how to tell them apart

head: The road
The circle
rows: The stretch has an end and a sign that you’ve arrived
The goal is “everything”, “the right life”, “when everything sorts itself out”
A turn changes the route, but not the destination
A new offer is judged by the course
A new offer is judged by its brightness
In an argument you look for a solution
In an argument you look for a convert
Companions can believe in something of their own
Companions must believe in the same thing
In a year you can show what has been done
In a year there is a new story about what will be

paragraphs: If more of your answers fall in the right-hand column, you are on the wheel. That is not a sentence: the wheel is part of the chariot; it needs not to be thrown away but to be set under the cart.

sections.h2: What to do with the 21-10-7 tail: eight practices
paragraphs: These are the author’s exercises, derived from the logic of the triple — not a rite and not a promise of results. Each one targets a specific link in the loop.

ol: **A stretch instead of the world.** Describe your picture of the whole in one sentence and put it aside: it is a horizon, not an address. Then name the nearest stretch of road — what will be done, by when, and by what sign you will know you have arrived. The crown is visible only at the end of the path, but the path can be seen right now.

**Three questions at a turn.** A new offer, a crisis, a failure or a bright idea — ask yourself: does this change the destination or only the road? Who is deciding now — me, my idea or the circumstances? What will I drop if I turn, and am I ready to drop it? These questions are the third move at the fork, between “push” and “wait”.

**A log of revolutions.** Write down five “new beginnings” from the last ten years: what began, at what turn it ended, where you ended up. Find the place where the same thing happens every time. That is your déjà vu, and it needs to be driven through differently, not all over again.

**Someone else’s faith in your own words.** Before arguing, restate the other person’s position so that they say: “Yes, that’s exactly what I think.” Only then say your own piece. This is the two-cups exercise: first pour from someone else’s.

**Say it once.** Offer your conviction once: what I think, why, what follows from it. After that the choice is the other person’s, and you can come back to the topic only if asked. A sermon differs from an opinion not in content but in the number of repeats.
**A daily move.** For the Wanderer mode: one small action on the chosen stretch every day, even fifteen minutes. The Chariot is not a decision made once but driving.

**What to bring back.** Before a move, a change of job, a new teacher or a new venture, answer in writing: what do I want to bring back from there? Travel for the sake of acquisition is a road. Travel with no answer to this question is an escape from a turn.

**Two cups.** When you are torn between two paths or two truths, don’t rush to throw one away. Ask what can be poured from one into the other: which skill from the past will be useful in the new, which part of someone else’s truth you can take into your own. Temperance in the centre is your tool, not your weakness.

paragraphs: And five phrases that break the script in the moment:

ul: Instead of “I know what’s right” — “this is what seems right to me”.
Instead of “it wasn’t meant to be” — “what will I do at this turn?”
Instead of “you have to understand” — “may I tell you how I see it?”
Instead of “I’ll start again from scratch” — “I’ll finish this stretch and then decide”.
Instead of “nobody understands me” — “who besides me needs this?”

sections.h2: The strength of 21-10-7: a guide through change
paragraphs: In its lived-through version this tail gives a rare combination. The person sees the whole (the World), knows how to move with change rather than against it (the Wheel), and sees what they have chosen through to the end (the Chariot). Add the centre — the ability to bring different things into harmony (Temperance) — and you get a guide: someone who leads people, a business or a family through changing circumstances towards a big goal and does not lose it at the turns.
Such people know how:

ul: **to hold the horizon and see the next step** — the big picture does not get in their way but helps them choose the stretches;
**to change the road without drama** — for them a turn is information, not a sign from above and not a betrayal;
**to join what can’t be joined** — people of different views, cultures and professions, old skills and new tasks;
**to persuade without preaching** — because they know how to pour from someone else’s cup first;
**to finish** — what they leave behind is not stories about what will be but finished sections of the road.

paragraphs: No list of “right” professions follows from this: you can be a guide in logistics, in a family, in science and in negotiations.

In Waite, the Chariot’s divinatory list does not begin with war at all. Its first words are “Succour, providence”, and war, triumph and vengeance come after the word “also”. The lived-through “warrior of faith” is the same chariot turned back to its first meaning: **a faith that does not fight but carries.**

sections.h2: How 21-10-7 differs from similar tails

head: Tail
What they share
Where they differ
rows: The same Chariot at the root; in popular readings both are “warriors”

12-19-7 fights under someone else’s banner for the sake of recognition, and has the Hierophant in the centre. 21-10-7 drives towards its own picture of the whole, with Temperance in the centre. There the question is “whose war is this”, here it is “where does this road lead”.
The same entry (the World) and the same middle (the Wheel)
At the root is the Tower: a form is held on to longer than it can stand, and it collapses. 21-10-7 often has no form to rebuild at all — only movement without a destination.
The World at the entry, the Wheel in the tail
There the Wheel stands at the root — it is the task, balance in motion. Here the Wheel is in the middle — it is the trap, the circle that the Chariot leads you out of.
The World and the Chariot in one tail
There the Chariot is the mechanism: the whole is taken by storm, and Death stands at the root. Here the Chariot is the root, the thing to learn: not to storm but to steer.

sections.h2: Myths about the 21-10-7 tail

ul: **“The Warrior of Faith is a religious fanatic.”** Faith here is any complete picture of how to live rightly. Many people with this tail are not religious at all and fight for a method, a politics, a way of raising children or the “right” kind of love.

**“A rare tail means a special soul with an important mission.”** The rarity is a consequence of arithmetic: days, months and years that add up to 7 or 52 are simply rare. There are no such dates at all in May, June and July, and there will be none from 2022 to 2029. Chosenness is not handed out that way.

**“Working with the tail means giving up your convictions.”** Temperance does not empty the cup; it needs two full ones: your own and someone else’s. And the root of the tail is the Chariot, which will not move without conviction.

**“The Wheel in the tail means life depends on luck.”** Waite saw behind this card precisely “the denial of chance and the fatality which is implied therein”. The Wheel here describes not luck but the habit of handing the steering to a turn or fighting it.
**“The tail promises moves and emigration.”** The tail does not assign events. It describes how a person deals with the road, not how many roads they will have.

**“In a past life you were an inquisitor or sold fakes.”** Such stories do not follow from the calculation and contradict each other: on some sites the tail comes from a preacher, on others from a seller of expired medicines. They cannot be checked, and they give nothing for the work.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: **Calculation** — Natalia Ladini’s classic destiny matrix scheme with points A–T: D = A + B + C, E = A + B + C + D, the tail M–N–D, where M = D + E and N = D + M; the relationship line M–R1–R, where L = C + E, R = L + M, R1 = M + R. Sums over 22 are reduced by adding their digits. The “7 or 52” condition, the constant centre 14, the full list of dates and the comparison with the relationship line were obtained by going through every day from 1900 to 2100; shares and frequency ranks were calculated from the dates of 1950–2025.

**Card meanings** — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, reissued 1922) with drawings by Pamela Colman Smith, and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Quotations are given in the original English. P. D. Ouspensky’s words on Temperance are given as quoted by Wen.

**The name “the Warrior of Faith” and the past-life legend** come from popular interpretations of the destiny matrix. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the matrix or karmic tails: assembling the three cards and the centre into one script is the author’s interpretation.

paragraphs: The destiny matrix is an esoteric system of interpretation, not a scientific method. The tail describes a tendency and gives you a language to notice it; it does not predict events, health or money.

sections.h2: This tail in compatibility
paragraphs: For a couple, 21-10-7 can be read as the search for a shared course amid many possibilities. The World at M concerns wishes to move beyond familiar limits; the Wheel of Fortune at N develops the task through changing conditions and openness to opportunities; the Chariot at D calls for agreement on direction and both people’s involvement. This is our editorial synthesis using Lisovskaya’s pair roles, rather than a separate description of the triple in her book.

The partners might discuss moving, studying or starting something together, only for each new offer to change the whole plan. Curiosity keeps the conversation alive while progress remains imaginary: yesterday’s decision gives way to today’s better option. At the other extreme, one person tires of choosing and declares their own route final. The Chariot gains speed at the expense of agreement, although the original wish belonged to both.

Choose one immediate stage, a deadline and the circumstances that would genuinely justify revisiting the decision. One person might investigate costs, the other conditions and limitations, before you discuss the findings together. The difficulty is confusing flexibility with endlessly changing the goal, or persistence with a ban on changing one’s mind. A shared course becomes steadier when new opportunities can be considered without automatically cancelling commitments already made.

faq.q: How do I know I have the 21-10-7 karmic tail?
faq.a: Add the arcanum of your birth day (30 → 3, 31 → 4), the number of the month and the reduced sum of the digits of the year. If you get exactly 7 or exactly 52, your tail is 21-10-7. In a ready chart the sign is even simpler: 14 in the centre. There is no other way to this tail.

faq.q: My chart has 21-10-7, but the centre is not 14. What is it?
faq.a: Most likely the triple stands in your relationship line M–R1–R. It occurs there four times as often as in the tail, and it is a different position: the script of a couple, not a karmic tail. In that case your tail is 21-4-10, 21-7-13 or 21-10-16. Look at the bottom ray of the chart, from the centre to the bottom corner: that is where the tail is written.

faq.q: Are 21-10-7 and 7-10-21 the same tail?
faq.a: Yes, if 7, 10 and 21 stand on the bottom ray of your chart: you are reading the tail from the corner to the centre. There is no tail that starts with 7 in this scheme — the first number is always a multiple of three. The triple 7-10-21 does not occur at all in the other lines of a personal chart, so “the 7-10-21 programme” is the same tail written in reverse order. The roles do not change: 21 is the entry, 10 the mechanism, 7 the root.

faq.q: Why is it so rare, and is it true that nobody gets it now?
faq.a: It is true. The sum 52 needs the largest numbers: a day from the 18th to the 22nd, a month no earlier than August, year digits adding up to 18 to 22. Years from 2000 to 2078 do not have such a sum. The sum 7 needs the smallest ones, and since 2022 even those are not small enough: the arcanum of 2022 is 6, and it only goes up from there. The next date with this tail is 1 January 2030, and after that 22 December 2079. That is why almost everyone who has it was born in 1953–1994 and 2000–2021.

faq.q: Why “the Warrior of Faith” if I am not religious?
faq.a: Because the faith in this name is any complete picture of “how it should be”. The name has a footing in the cards: in Waite’s divinatory list the Chariot has war, and Temperance reversed, which stands in the centre for everyone with this tail, has churches, religions, sects and competing interests. The plot of the tail is not about religion but about what a person does with their truth: fights for it, waits for life to confirm it, or drives their own road with it.

faq.q: I found 21-10-7 in a compatibility matrix. Is it the same tail?
faq.a: No. A compatibility matrix is built from two dates, and the triple in it describes the shared script of a couple. The partners keep their own personal tails, each their own. A triple from a compatibility chart has to be read by the rules of that scheme; the reading above is about a personal chart.

faq.q: Is the tail different for men and women?
faq.a: No. Sex plays no part in the calculation and changes neither the numbers nor the mechanism. A person of any sex can turn out to be a Crusader or a Wanderer; only the circumstances in which the script shows itself differ.

faq.q: Can the 21-10-7 tail be closed?
faq.a: The numbers in the chart do not change; what changes is how the script is played out. Signs of a lived-through tail: your road has a nearest stretch with a finish line; you meet a turn with a question, not with war or submission; you can retell someone else’s truth so that its author agrees; what you leave behind are finished sections of the road, not just started ones.

head: Position
Arcanum
Role in the script
Image
rows: a picture of the whole: “I know how everything should be”
a garland that Lévi called a crown
a turn after which everything starts over
choose your own stretch of road and drive it yourself
the same for everyone with this tail: measure, harmony, “both at once”
a path to a barely visible crown
